title: Russell Westbrook Gets Surprise Retirement Twist as One NBA Voice Hints at Heat Return
description: Russell Westbrook walked away from the NBA last month after 18 seasons, closing a career that produced an MVP award, nine All-Star selections and the league’s all-time triple-double record. Since then, though, his retirement has not stopped people around basketball from wondering whether he could change his mind. The speculation has come from different corners [...]
fullText:
Russell Westbrook walked away from the NBA last month after 18 seasons, closing a career that produced an MVP award, nine All-Star selections and the league's all-time triple-double record. Since then, though, his retirement has not stopped people around basketball from wondering whether he could change his mind.

The speculation has come from different corners of the basketball world. Some have pointed to his recent production, while others have focused on the fact that he still looked capable of contributing before deciding to leave the league.

The latest name to reopen the conversation is former NBA All-Star Zach Randolph. During an episode of the Out the Mud podcast with Tony Allen, Randolph suggested Westbrook could return and named the Miami Heat as a team he would like to see him join.

"I'd like to see him with the Heat. Brodie got a lot left in him. I just saw his little brother yesterday Ray. He might be back."

Randolph's comments do not indicate that Miami has contacted Westbrook. They also do not establish that Westbrook is considering another NBA season. The 37-year-old announced his retirement on Aug. 12 and has made no public statement reversing that decision.

The Heat suggestion adds another layer to a discussion that had already begun before Randolph spoke.

Former Lakers teammate Patrick Beverley recently argued that Westbrook still had several NBA seasons left. Beverley suggested the veteran guard could remain in the league for another three or four years and also discussed Miami as a potential destination.

That comment came despite Westbrook's own retirement announcement. Beverley's opinion also carried a personal connection because he played alongside Westbrook with the Lakers during the 2022-23 season.

The comeback talk actually started almost immediately after Westbrook retired.

Ice Cube publicly invited Westbrook to continue playing in the BIG3 just one day after the announcement. The league founder argued that fans still wanted to see the nine-time All-Star play, even if he was no longer doing it in the NBA.

Former teammate Kevin Durant also said Westbrook's retirement surprised him because he believed his longtime running mate could still play. Durant's comments were more about Westbrook's ability than a prediction that he would return, but they added to the feeling that the decision came while he still had something left.

Westbrook's final NBA season gives that discussion some context. Playing for Sacramento, he averaged 15.2 points, 6.7 assists and 5.4 rebounds across 64 games while starting 58 times. He finished his career with 209 triple-doubles, a record that still stands.

There is still no confirmed comeback plan. For now, the Heat connection belongs to Randolph, while Beverley and others have simply kept the possibility alive.

Westbrook remains retired. Yet, less than two months after his final season, the basketball world is still leaving room for one more chapter.

title: Kawhi Leonard Gets Special Raptors Welcome From Former No. 3 Pick
description: Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto seven years after delivering the franchise its first NBA championship. His return carries a different meaning for one Raptors player who was still a fan when Leonard’s biggest Toronto moment happened. That player was not yet in the NBA at the time. He was preparing for the draft, watching [...]
fullText:
Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto seven years after delivering the franchise its first NBA championship. His return carries a different meaning for one Raptors player who was still a fan when Leonard's biggest Toronto moment happened.

That player was not yet in the NBA at the time. He was preparing for the draft, watching the Raptors make history while hoping to join the league himself someday.

The former No. 3 pick is RJ Barrett, a Toronto-area native who was preparing for the 2019 NBA Draft when the Raptors captured the title.

Barrett remembers that championship run differently from most players now entering Toronto's locker room. He was not part of the organization yet, but he was following every game as a lifelong Raptors supporter.

"I've been a Raptors fan my whole life. I was getting ready for the NBA Draft when the Raptors won the championship. When he made that Game 7 shot against Philly, I was jumping up-and-down like crazy," said Barrett.

RJ Barrett is HYPED to team up with Kawhi Leonard:

“I’ve been a Raptors fan my whole life. I was getting ready for the NBA Draft when the Raptors won the championship. When he made that Game 7 shot against Philly, I was jumping up-and-down like crazy.”

(via @cbcsports, h/t… pic.twitter.com/3dUuLDEK2A

— Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) September 20, 2026

Leonard's shot against Philadelphia remains one of the most recognizable moments in Raptors history. The four-bounce jumper sent Toronto into the Eastern Conference finals, and Leonard eventually led the team through the championship run while winning Finals MVP.

Barrett entered the NBA weeks later, going third overall to the New York Knicks. Toronto eventually brought him home in the December 2023 trade that sent him from New York to the Raptors.

That makes Leonard's return feel different from a normal reunion. Barrett went from watching him as a teenager to preparing to share the floor with him as an established NBA player.

There is an even more unusual link between the two players. During Toronto's 2026 playoff series against Cleveland, Barrett created his own memorable moment at Scotiabank Arena. He hit a three-pointer with 1.2 seconds left in overtime of Game 6, and the ball bounced high off the rim before dropping through to give the Raptors a 112-110 victory. The win forced a deciding Game 7.

The resemblance to Leonard's 2019 shot was hard to miss.

Leonard's famous attempt had bounced four times before falling through. Barrett's shot hit the heel of the rim and bounced more than 10 feet into the air before dropping.

Barrett's game-winning shot in Game 6 was strikingly similar to Leonard's famous shot from 2019. Leonard's shot bounced four times before going in, while Barrett's shot hit the rim and bounced more than 10 feet into the air, almost reaching the top of the shot clock, before falling through the net.

This left only 1.2 seconds on the clock. Leonard's buzzer-beater broke a tie in Game 7, but Barrett's shot saved his team from losing by one point and secured the Game 6 victory.

The situations were different, but the setting created an unusual connection between the two moments. One shot became the defining image of Toronto's first championship run. The other kept the Raptors alive in a playoff series seven years later.

Now those two moments belong to players on the same team.

Toronto officially completed Leonard's return on September 14, acquiring him from the Los Angeles Clippers for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, a first-round swap and two second-round picks.

Leonard also returns as a very different player from the one Barrett watched in 2019. He averaged a career-high 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists in 65 games last season.

For Barrett, the statistics take a back seat to the memories. He was just about to enter the NBA when Leonard hit that iconic shot. Now, the player he once admired as a Raptors fan has become his teammate.

description: The Atlanta Hawks will return for training camp in about a week, but they won’t have one of their rookies after suffering a major injury. Second-round pick Henri Veesaar will miss the season with a torn ACL, according to the team. “During a workout on Sept. 15, center Henri Veesaar sustained a right knee injury. Following an MRI and evaluation at […] The post Hawks news: Atlanta loses rookie center to torn ACL days before training camp appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Hawks news: Atlanta loses rookie center to torn ACL days before training camp appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Atlanta Hawks will return for training camp in about a week, but they won't have one of their rookies after suffering a major injury. Second-round pick Henri Veesaar will miss the season with a torn ACL, according to the team.

"During a workout on Sept. 15, center Henri Veesaar sustained a right knee injury. Following an MRI and evaluation at the Emory Sports Medicine Complex, he was diagnosed with a torn right ACL. Veesaar will undergo surgery with Dr. Kyle Hammond at the Emory Sports Medicine Complex in October and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season," the team said in a press release.

Veesaar was drafted by the Hawks with the 52nd pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. There was a good chance that Veesaar wasn't going to play many minutes for the Hawks this season, with their center depth already strong, and he would've seen most of his time in the G League with the College Park Skyhawks.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Veesaar has several skills that can help him make an impact on the floor, especially with the Hawks. He can stretch the floor with his shooting, as well as rebound at a high level. His playmaking skills are underrated, and he can make passes that most centers probably couldn't.

Going into the season, the Hawks will have Onyeka Okongwu and Jock Landale on their roster, and they'll have most of the minutes at the position. It'll be interesting to see if the Hawks decide to add another center to the roster before training camp.

title: Eagles TE Dallas Goedert reportedly expected to miss multiple weeks with sprained MCL
description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert sustained a sprained MCL in Sunday’s win over the Tennessee Titans and is expected to miss multiple weeks, ESPN reports.
fullText:
Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert sustained a sprained MCL in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans and is expected to miss multiple weeks, ESPN reports.

Goedert, 31, is a ninth-season NFL veteran who's played for the Eagles for his entire career. He's been one of the league's most reliable producers at his position throughout his career and remains a key piece of Philadelphia's offense as its No. 1 tight end.

Goedert's a favorite red-zone target of quarterback Jalen Hurts and a standout blocker for a run game that struggled on Sunday after his exit and a stinger to starting running back Saquon Barkley that limited him to four carries. The Eagles tallied 89 yards on 32 carries (2.8 yards per carry) against the Titans.

Through two games this season, Goedert has 5 catches for 81 yards and 2 touchdowns, with both scores coming against Washington in Week 1. Goedert was limited to one catch on Sunday before leaving the game with injury before halftime.

Goedert tallied a career-high 11 touchdowns on 60 catches for 591 yards last season.

The Eagles are off to a 2-0 start, but struggled to put away a bad Titans team on Monday. They trailed, 20-17 late in the fourth quarter before scoring a touchdown to secure the winning final margin.

title: ACU football’s Brandon Perez earns UAC Specialist of the Week honors
description: ACU senior kicker Brandon Perez was named the United Athletic Conference Specialist of the Week for his role in the Wildcats' 41-39 win over Idaho.
fullText:
Abilene Christian senior kicker Brandon Perez has been named the United Athletic Conference's Specialist of the Week following the Wildcats' 41-39 road win over the Idaho Vandals on Saturday.

He was a perfect 5-for-5 on PAT kicks and drilled a pair of field goals — including a career long 51-yard field goal kick — to help lift ACU to its first win of the season in a back-and-forth game against Idaho.

Perez — a former Crandall High School football standout who transferred to ACU from East Central University, an NCAA Division II school in Ada, Oklahoma — took over as Abilene Christian's starting kicker three games into the 2025 season.

Since taking the reins as the Wildcats' kicker, Perez has been one of the country's most consistent kickers at the FCS level.

He has converted on 54 of 55 PAT kicks since arriving at Abilene Christian and boasts an 18-of-24 mark on field goal attempts in 17 career games played for the Wildcats.

Perez provided ACU with a signature moment during the 2025 season when he drilled a game-winning 47-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Wildcats to a 31-28 victory over then-No. 2 ranked rival Tarleton State.

title: “I’m going to lose it” – Chelsea player’s biggest flaw in new position has pundit furious
description: Pedro Neto is a controversial player with many Chelsea fans, and his latest performance was another masterclass in frustration.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as ...
fullText:
Pedro Neto is a controversial player with many Chelsea fans, and his latest performance was another masterclass in frustration.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

There is plenty of blame to go round after Chelsea conceded yet more soft goals and went a third game without a win on Friday night.

Lots of players have been criticised, and on the London is Blue podcast, presetner Nick Verlaney set his sights on winger Pedro Neto.

Neto has been playing as a right wing back, but as a left footer that means he's less able to pass down the line or go on the outside of a defender. Verlaney is tired of the limitations of that.

LONDON, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 09: Pedro Neto of Chelsea celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on September 09, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

"I almost think he needs to play as a left wing back moving forward, because if I have to see him shift the ball from his right foot, where he clearly doesn't want to pass it, I'm going to lose it," the presentersaid.

"Every defender in the league knows he's not gonna use his right foot. He's going to try and cut it back, do the little dance thing to try and create space for himself. He's going to try and take four shots from outside the box.

"Not only that, he was terrible defensively in this game. He was caught not tracking back a couple of times, which I thought we were over, from an attitude perspective."

Chelsea's xG stats put them in the bottom quarter of the league – and they've conceded more goals than anyone. It's a worrying stat to consider in the international break.

A bitterly frustrated Xabi Alonso criticised his team's mentality in much the same way we've seen a few managers criticise it in recent years.

description: The (0-2) Atlanta Falcons play the (1-1) Green Bay Packers on the road at Lambeau Field for Thursday Night Football. Cooper Rush started the first two games because the effective starter Tua Tagovailoa was out with a back injury. fullText:
The (0-2) Atlanta Falcons play the (1-1) Green Bay Packers on the road at Lambeau Field for Thursday Night Football. One interesting storyline surrounding the Week 3 contest is who will start at quarterback. Cooper Rush started the first two games because the effective starter Tua Tagovailoa was out with a back injury. However, Rush was benched in the third quarter in favor of Bloomer, Wisconsin native and undrafted rookie Jack Strand.

In addition, Michael Penix Jr. missed the first two games while recovering from a partial ACL tear sustained in November. This was Penix's third ACL tear and the first sustained to his left knee. He was cleared for full-team, 11-on-11 drills on August 22 but wanted to pass a physical hurdle before he could play.

"I'm close. I'm close," Penix said last Wednesday, via Will McFadden of the team's website. "I know I've been saying that, but there's just a couple of technical things that I want to hit, some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do stuff out on that field. But I do feel really good, and we're taking strides each and every day.

"I would say more physical goals," Penix said. "As far as mental, it ain't even mental. Mentally, I want to go play. But I'm not going to go out there if I don't feel where I need to be physically."

On X, the Falcons announced they have named Michael Penix Jr. the starting quarterback against the Packers on Thursday Night Football. As a result, Penix will make his regular-season debut in hopes of becoming the team's starting quarterback of the future. In addition, Atlanta hopes to reach the opponent's red zone after failing to do so in its first 25 drives of the first two games.

title: Liverpool eyeing move for Arne Slot favourite who Arsenal also want
description: Arne Slot's time as Liverpool manager came to a bit of an abrupt end. Just a season after winning the Premier League title, the Dutchman was relieved of his duties due to the poor performances that hi...
fullText:
Arne Slot's time as Liverpool manager came to a bit of an abrupt end.

Just a season after winning the Premier League title, the Dutchman was relieved of his duties due to the poor performances that his men were putting in.

The Reds did a terrible job of trying to defend their top flight title as they only finished fifth in the league.

And, to make things worse, they only got to the round of 16 in the Champions League.

All of these things combined together to make fans believe that another massive rebuild was on its way to Anfield.

Four players ended up getting brought in during the summer but, since there are still a couple of glaring problems among their ranks, some more transfers are needed.

Of course, the January transfer window is still quite a few months away yet but, that hasn't stopped the rumour mill from turning.

When Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool last summer, everyone knew that he would be difficult to replace.

The right-back was one of the Reds' most creative players and, even though Jeremie Frimpong was brought in to replace him, he has not managed to meet expectations.

This led to Liverpool signing Ronald Araujo on loan in the 2026-27 summer transfer window with a €55 million option to buy and, while he's been incredible so far, the €55 million option to buy still feels a bit steep.

Indeed, without the Uruguayan, the Reds would be in a much worse position than they currently find themselves but, since he's going to be 28 years old by June 2027, he's a tad older than Liverpool's usual targets.

So, this has forced the rumour mill to start turning about other potential right-backs that Liverpool could explore and, thanks to an update from Ekrem Konur, one of the Reds' previous targets seems to have re-entered the frame.

Depending on how good Conor Bradley is upon his return from injury, Liverpool's right-back could quickly become another massive issue for them in the future.

At the moment, with Joe Gomez, Frimpong and Araujo all available, they're fairly well covered at right-back but, if another injury crisis makes its way over to L4, they could be in some serious trouble.

And, if Liverpool don't end up activating their option to buy on Araujo, their main right-back for the 2026-27 season will be taken away from them.

Read has only ever played in the Eredivisie with Slot being the manager to hand him his debut for Feyenoord.

Not only did he quickly become one of the Dutchman's favourite players but, he also proved how good he is.

So far this season, the defender has featured in eight games across all competitions and he already has five assists to his name which, for a 20-year-old is very impressive.

Obviously, a deal for the right-back wouldn't be cheap but, if Liverpool think he's the next Alexander-Arnold, he'll be worth every penny.

title: Miami Dolphins' Jeff Hafley updates Caleb Douglas, Chop Robinson
description: The Miami Dolphins are dealing with injuries to Caleb Douglas, Jaylen Wright and Chon Robinson.
fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley met with reporters a day after the 35-13 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, dropping the team to 0-2.

On receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle): Too early to tell on if he might play Sunday. We'll see how that goes.

Edge Chop Robinson has made progress in concussion protocol. "He's exactly where we though he'd be right now."

RB Jaylen Wright (stinger) is day to day. They'll see how he does Wednesday.

On punter Bradley Pinion: "He's never dropped a ball like that before and I'm sure he won't do it again."

On RT Austin Jackson: He went against Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa, two of the better pass rushers in the league, and the Dolphins could have helped Jackson more. "He's had some good moments and some moments just like the rest of us."

Hafley says when you turn on the tape, you see an element of toughness that "jumps off the tape, and that's really important to me." Hafley says the team is playing just as hard at the end of the game as the start.

Hafley said the run defense was "cleaned up" vs. the 49ers.

On Malik Willis: "There's moments when the ball's out on time, he's been able to extend plays. He's accurate. ... It's the consistency level right now (that needs work). Those are things early in the year, that a lot of quarterbacks are working on right now."

On whether coaches are considering lineup changes: "I'd be lying to you if I didn't say there were those conversations."

On the issues in the secondary vs. the 49ers: Communication was the problem. "We had some busts I haven't seen, haven't seen in camp, and we need to communicate more. ... Clearly that was the biggest issue yesterday."

On the penalties: Some are lack of focus, some involves a player getting beat and grabbing him. "Every time we crossed the 40-yard line yesterday, we were put in tough situations." Hafley added, "It's not an excuse. Not anymore. We're in Week 3."

Hafley said he had "a great one-on-one talk" with veteran receiver Jalen Tolbert, who has been inactive the first two weeks. "His time will come. I have a great admiration and appreciation for how he's handled it."

Hal Habib covers the Miami Dolphins for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at HHabib@usatodayco.com.

title: ‘People Around the League Will Be Monitoring’ — NBA Insiders Make Feelings Clear on Kyrie Irving’s Uncertain Future With Mavericks
description: The Dallas Mavericks might have to make a decision regarding their veteran star soon. The team already has the new face of its franchise in Cooper Flagg, which places Kyrie Irving’s future with the team into question.
fullText:
The Dallas Mavericks might have to make a decision regarding their veteran star soon. The team already has the new face of its franchise in Cooper Flagg, which places Kyrie Irving's future with the team into question.

NBA Insiders Tim MacMahon and Marc J. Spears discussed the future and the uncertainties surrounding it.

The 2025-26 season proved that the hype surrounding Flagg is legitimate. Through 70 games, he averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 4.5 assists on his way to winning the Rookie of the Year award.

The 6-foot-9 forward showed that he could be the Mavericks' franchise cornerstone for a very long time. Still, his emergence does not make the team contenders just yet. Having him simply means they already know who to build around. However, they are likely several years and multiple pieces away from being a title threat.

The Mavericks' current state does not align with Irving's career, given that he is already 34. He can neither wait for Flagg to become a bona fide superstar nor for the Mavericks to find the right pieces to surround him with.

Since their timelines are not in sync, MacMahon believes several teams will keep an eye on this situation. The league insider acknowledged on Monday's episode of "NBA Today" that Irving is still the team's veteran leader. However, that might not be the case for long.

"The question that's being asked around the league is 'for how long?'" MacMahon said. "How long is this fit with Kyrie and the Mavericks?"

MacMahon clarified that the reason is that Flagg is now the team's centerpiece, and not because Irving and the Mavericks no longer see eye to eye.

"Would it make sense for both sides to find a contender for Kyrie to go to?" MacMahon continued. "These are the kind of things that people around the league will be monitoring leading up to the trade deadline."

Spears later added that if they decided to move on from each other, it would be an amicable split. He highlighted the strong relationship between Irving and Mavericks president Masai Ujiri as the reason for this.

"Masai also has a really good relationship, with Kyrie Irving," Spears said. "I think it's the kind of relationship where if Kyrie says, 'hey Masai, like this isn't for me,' I think they could work together to get something done."

Irving has not played a game since March 2025. He suffered a torn ACL near the end of the 2024-25 season, which also kept him out of action for the entirety of last season. He is expected to return this upcoming season, but an exact schedule for it has yet to be officially announced.

Once the nine-time All-Star returns, there's no doubt that he could elevate the Mavericks. He is one of the league's most proficient offensive weapons, and he can take defensive pressure off Flagg.

MORE: 'The Sky Is the Limit' – Mavericks Legend Dirk Nowitzki Details How Cooper Flagg Can Follow In His Footsteps

With Irving running the point, the Mavericks would have someone to keep the team steady through difficult stretches. However, staying could mean sacrificing a chance to add another championship ring to his extensive collection of awards and accolades.

title: Falcons list 9 players on estimated injury report to begin Week 3
description: Falcons release estimated injury report: 9 players listed to begin Week 3
fullText:

However, Penix was just named the starting quarterback for Thursday's prime-time showdown in Green Bay, so we wouldn't worry about him being listed. Tagovailoa was limited with an oblique injury, but that's actually an improvement for the veteran QB, who was held out of the last four practices.

Aside from the quarterbacks, the Falcons listed two key players as non-participants on their simulated Monday practice report. Edge rusher Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and cornerback A.J. Terrell (groin) were absent to start Week 3, but we can't read to much into that since the team didn't actually practice.

Right tackle Jawaan Taylor, defensive end Brandon Dorlus, tight end Nick Muse and running back Brian Robinson Jr. were listed as limited on Monday. Check out the Falcons' full estimated injury report below.

DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring): DNP

QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique): LP

The Falcons will look to Penix to lead them out their first win of the season after a brutal 0-2 start. Thursday's game starts at 8:15 p.m. ET at Lambeau Field in Green Bay.

title: T.J. Watt’s Odds to Win Annual NFL Award Continue to Rise
description: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt may just add to his hardware collection this season.
fullText:
Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt may just add to his hardware collection this season.

Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt had yet another impressive showing against the New England Patriots in Week 2. That's exactly why his odds of winning this year's NFL Defensive Player of the Year award continue to rise.

According to Kalshi Sports, Watt now has the best odds (21%) to win the 2026 DPOY award, tied with Detroit Lions Aidan Hutchinson. That's up 9% from a week ago when he was third in the rankings.

NFL Week 2 DPOY Power Rankings, via Kalshi:

1. Aidan Hutchinson (21%)
2. TJ Watt (21%)
3. Will Anderson Jr (16%)
4. Fred Warner (14%)
5. Abdul Carter (7%)
6. Nick Bosa (6%)
7. Maxx Crosby (5%)
8. Trey Hendrickson (4%)
9. Nik Bonitto (3%)
10. Greg Rosseau (3%) pic.twitter.com/ztaGvySLZb

— Kalshi Sports (@KalshiSports) September 21, 2026

Watt has certainly started off his 2026 campaign strong. After recording four tackles, two sacks, one pass defensed, one interception and one touchdown in Week 1, he followed it up with another four tackles and 1.5 sacks in Week 2.

That puts Watt on par with or even better than Hutchinson, who has racked up eight tackles, three sacks and one forced fumble through the first two weeks of the regular season.

The only question is if Watt can continue producing at this level all season. Many didn't even believe Watt had very much good football left in him, coming off one of the worst seasons of his career.

In 2025, Watt had just seven sacks after having double digit sack totals in six of his last seven seasons.

However, the 2021 NFL Defensive Player of the Year now seems as determined as ever to prove his doubters wrong and earn his second such award, even if he continues splitting time with fellow outside linebackers Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig.

A first-round pick in the 2017 NFL Draft, Watt has recorded 525 tackles, 118.5 sacks, 36 forced fumbles, 14 fumble recoveries, 59 passes defensed, 10 interceptions and one touchdown in his professional career.

title: Jayden Daniels injury: Fantasy football impact with Marcus Mariota expected to start Week 3
description: The Washington Commanders will once again have to play without Jayden Daniels, as he suffered a dislocated left shoulder against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. Daniels is expected to undergo imaging today and will talk to several experts over the next few days to see what the next steps will be for him. There’s no telling when Daniels will return to […] The post Jayden Daniels injury: Fantasy football impact with Marcus Mariota expected to start Week 3 appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Jayden Daniels injury: Fantasy football impact with Marcus Mariota expected to start Week 3 appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Washington Commanders will once again have to play without Jayden Daniels, as he suffered a dislocated left shoulder against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. Daniels is expected to undergo imaging today and will talk to several experts over the next few days to see what the next steps will be for him. There's no telling when Daniels will return to the field, but for the time being, Marcus Mariota is set to be the starter.

The Commanders have seen a lot of Mariota over the past year after Daniels dealt with several injuries last season. There's no question that he's familiar with the system, but things will be a bit different with him controlling the offense and not Daniels.

Fantasy-wise, it's hard to see many of their key players on offense see a rise in their numbers with Mariota. Terry McLaurin will probably see a dip in his numbers, as well as Stefon Diggs, but it could simply depend on the matchups during the week. Mariota may find a safety blanket within the passing game, and Diggs is known as a possession receiver.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Diggs had a good game against the Dallas Cowboys, and he could continue that if Mariota keeps finding him for however long he's QB1.

There's a good chance that Mariota relies on the run a lot, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt's fantasy numbers could see a rise. Whether that's out of the backfield or dumping it off to him in the flats, Croskey-Merritt may see a lot of work in the offense for the next few weeks.

As for Mariota himself, no one is expecting him to come in and have big performances every week. It's a plus that he can use his legs like Daniels, but his impact just won't be the same. It might be best for fantasy owners to stay away from Commanders players until Daniels returns so they can get the best out of them.

title: How a Major Storm Could Impact End of Regular Season, Playoff Seeding For Red Sox
description: Mother Nature may not cooperate with what appears to be a massive series at the end of Boston's 2026 regular-season schedule.
fullText:
How a Major Storm Could Impact End of Regular Season, Playoff Seeding For Red Sox originally appeared on NESN. 

With a postseason bid secured, the Red Sox still have work to do in deciding their spot in the AL bracket. But with only two series remaining in their regular season, there's limited time remaining before October.

Boston's penultimate regular season series begins Tuesday against the Guardians, but on Friday, the Red Sox will host the Cubs at Fenway Park to conclude their 2026 schedule. Those three games, in all likelihood, will carry significant implications on both sides of the MLB postseason bracket.

Mother Nature may not cooperate with the Red Sox-Cubs series, though. On Sunday night, a viral social media post showed a significant storm brewing for the weekend in the New England area, something that could disrupt a critical season-concluding series.

Here's why a storm could throw off this weekend's Red Sox series against the Cubs.

Late in the upcoming week, in the Northeast, a potentially significant storm could be brewing.

According to NBC 10 Boston, by Friday and Saturday, a storm "will start to churn off the mid-Atlantic coast. As it deepens and gathers strength, it will also back northwest towards New England," and models indicate it will bring "strong wind, heavy rain, and possible coastal flooding."

I can't stress enough how messy the Cubs and Red Sox situation is about to get if anything close to a storm like this comes to fruition next weekend (a high likelihood given the blocking pattern in eastern Canada).

The Red Sox are virtually locked into the second AL Wild Card… pic.twitter.com/E4jKktW63x

The Red Sox are scheduled to host the Cubs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. While Boston has already secured a postseason bid and Chicago is on the verge of doing so, the series could still hold implications for seeding, making it unlikely MLB would cancel games altogether.

If the weather does prove disruptive, it could force MLB to schedule a doubleheader between the Red Sox and Cubs, similar to the Mets-Braves series in 2024.

Another option, while unfavorable, is making up the games next Monday, which would put the two teams at a rest disadvantage heading into the postseason.

Plenty of time for the forecast to change, but the Red Sox are looking at potentially needing to make up one or two Cubs games next Monday, the day before the playoffs start.

title: EU plans "digital expropriation" of Europeans in the interest of AI companies
description: In a leaked document, the Irish Presidency proposes to EU Member States that the interest of AI companies to make profits should take precedence over the fundamental rights of Europeans.
fullText:
In a leaked document, the Irish Presidency proposes to EU Member States that the interest of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to make profits should take precedence over the fundamental right to data protection. Use of personal data “in the context of AI” should automatically be lawful. There seems to be wide informal agreement by many Member States. In particular, Big Tech would be able to use all personal data collected over the past decades with virtually no restrictions, as long as this happens “in the context” of AI. Schrems: “Under these proposals, the profits of AI companies would trump European’s fundamental right to privacy. This is nothing but a digital expropriation of Europeans.” All this is happening despite the key figures of AI corporations actively warn about the enormous risks associated with their own products.

Last limits fall: Profits of AI companies trump data protection? As part of the Digital Omnibus Proposal, the European Commission claimed to adopt only minor simplifications for EU companies, whilst explicitly claiming to maintain a “high level of protection” for Europeans. As the changes were intended to be minimal, a “fast-track procedure” was chosen - without any fundamental rights assessment and without directly involving the European expert group on data protection.

Article 88c proposed by the European Commission (now Article 88bis in the Council document) intends to liberate the use of personal data for AI. The proposal is currently with the Council, where the Irish Presidency currently holds the reins. Ireland serves as the EU headquarter for the majority of the US and China’s AI corporations.

With support of Germany and other EU powerhouses, it is currently proposed, that, when using personal data “in the context of AI”, companies are generally permitted to do basically anything. The commercial interests of AI companies should generally trump the fundamental rights of users. This general allowance would also apply to individuals who have never been customers of an AI company, or to data entered decades ago, for example in chats or on social media. All personal data that an AI company can somehow get its hands on would fall under the provision. There is no need to ask users for consent – companies are automatically assumed to have an overriding “legitimate interest” if they train or use any AI product.

Schrems: “A likely majority of EU member states are now saying that the interests of Elon Musk, Marc Zuckerberg, Google or Open AI, in making enormous profits, should take precedence over European’s fundamental right to data protection. This is nothing short of the ‘digital expropriation’ of Europeans. Everything we have ever entered into digital systems, or that AI corporations have otherwise obtained, becomes fair game for AI corporations to use.”

The sale of European data to the US and China. Politicians seem to believe, that the European economy will benefit from the abolishment of as many laws as possible. Nonetheless, the exact opposite can be expected: most EU companies neither have the access to the same volume of data, nor the capital to compete with US corporations. In many cases, this could also mean that the data collected by EU companies (but processed on platforms or services in the US) would flow to providers in the US or China.

Schrems: “This legislative change primarily benefits the big players, those who have collected massive amounts of European’s data. This is a complete sell-off of European data to global corporations. It would also result in a large amount of know-how flowing from EU companies to the US or China. From an industrial policy perspective, such an approach is madness.”

A blank check for an entire technology? Usually, the GDPR permits processing for specific purposes (e.g. retention for tax records or fraud prevention). However, the currently proposed Article 88c (or Article 88bis) legitimises an entire technology. Regardless of the purpose for which it is used, any AI system would be lawfully sucking up any personal data by default. For example, the proposed Article would also permit the training and use of AI for manipulation, disinformation, the generation of nude images, or killer drones and indeed any other questionable purpose. Many processing operations that were so far illegal would suddenly become legal – just because they are done “in the context” of an AI system. For example, data processing for personal advertising purposes (without consent) is currently illegal in the EU. Now however, if advertising is to be personalised using AI technology, it would suddenly become legal.

Schrems: “It’s like saying anything goes — no matter what you do — as long as it’s done with a specific technology. Many things that were previously illegal would suddenly be legal, as long as you use AI. It is utterly absurd to give a high-risk technology preferential treatment over every other computer system.”

The 45-year promise of data protection is collapsing. On a European level, data protection legislation has existed since 1981. For decades, Europeans have been promised that such (supposedly) “strict” data protection, would ensure that platforms such as Twitter/X, Facebook or Instagram, and corporations such as Google or Microsoft which collect vast amounts of data, would “never” use it for other purposes that for what they were shared. The proposed Article 88c (or now 88bis) breaks this promise: all collected data is suddenly up for grabs, for any use, by any AI system.

Schrems: “Since the 1980s, we have promised people that whilst large corporations may hold onto the data, they are only permitted to use it to a limited extent. Article 88bis now suddenly throws open the floodgates, and allows unlimited use of all data for AI.”

Further massive limitations on protections and rights. The EU member states have further proposed drastically narrowing the definition of “personal data”, meaning that, amongst other things, it is unclear whether, for example, online tracking would still be covered by the GDPR. This is meant to be done via so-called "pseudonyms" that should regularly not be covered by the GDPR anymore. The problem is, that most IT systems primarily work with pseudonyms (such as user IDs, tracking IDs, IP addresses or social security numbers).

Furthermore, internal company knowledge and capabilities should be an element to be taken into account to determine if the GDPR even applies. Equally, data subject rights should not be applicable if they are “abused” by a data subject.

In practice, these "subjective" factors are prone to abuse. The decision of whether data is still “personal” or a right is “abusive” would be primarily made by the companies that are regulated by the law. Both of these measures can make it almost impossible to enforce the GDPR in practice. In each individual case, companies could have lengthy debates about their (unknown) internal capabilities and intentions and speculate about the potentially "abusive" intentions of users. Such debates typically drag on for years and drown procedures in enormous delays and enormous costs - so anything but "simplification".

Schrems: “These changes are right from the playbook of any big law firm defending big tech. We spend years in courts and before authorities to get these claims rejected. The EU legislator will likely turbocharge them and hence make EU law even more complex and unenforceable.”

Position of the European Commission and the European Parliament. The European Commission made a 180-degree turn a while ago, and currently clearly prioritises the interests of industry lobbies over fundamental rights. The position of the European Parliament remains mixed. Whilst most of the European People’s Party tend to argue in favour of putting more and more loopholes in EU digital laws, Members of the European Parliament, from the centre-left factions have so far pushed back. Increasingly also far-rights groups oppose proposals for a “free pass” for Big Tech.

Last hope: The Court of Justice? The main question seems to be whether a law without any meaningful restrictions can in any way be reconciled with EU fundamental rights. In the past, the European Court of Justice has struck down EU law in cases involving much less significant infringements of EU fundamental rights, such as data retention or the transfer of EU data to the United States.

Schrems: “If the legislator has lost all sense of proportion and direction, then the people can only turn to the courts. Any extreme law that has a high risk of being overturned would at the same time only create more legal uncertainty – instead of promised simplification.”

title: A Major Cold Intrusion Spreads Across Eastern Europe: Seasonal Frost to Follow
description: Explore the impact of the cold air mass sweeping across Eastern Europe and bringing the first autumn frost.
fullText:
The main driver of this rapid thermal drop this week is a massive upper-level blocking ridge building over the North Atlantic and Scandinavia. This high-pressure area is forcing a direct atmospheric corridor for meridional flow from the north, allowing dense, polar-origin air to spill deep across Eastern Europe.

As the cold front pushes south, daytime high temperatures across impacted regions will plunge by 10 to 15 °C compared to recent seasonal averages.

As the polar air mass settles over the region, clear nocturnal skies and lighter winds will support first morning frost across low-lying valleys and agricultural basins from the Baltic countries down to the central Balkans, reaching Romania and Bulgaria. Across the higher elevations of the Carpathians and possibly the Northern Balkans, falling freezing levels will trigger the first notable high-altitude snowfalls of the autumn season.

While the cold intrusion will last only through the mid-week days, it will be significant for the second half of September. The meteogram charts for Niš, Serbia (upper) and Istanbul, Turkey (bottom) both show a sharp temperature drop on Tuesday and Wednesday.

The following forecast model animations and 850 hPa temperature anomaly maps below illustrate the progression of this Arctic air mass across the eastern half of the continent, highlighting where the most severe thermal anomalies and early-season freeze risks will focus over the coming days.

Let’s dig into the details of this significant pattern change that is temporarily ending the return of warmth over Eastern Europe this week.

The general weather picture over the North Atlantic and European continent this week shows a strong upper-level ridge over Western and Southwestern Europe, expanding toward Northern Europe as a Scandinavian High develops. A large upper-level wave is emerging into Eastern Europe on Tuesday. It is spreading south through midweek, reaching as far south as the southern Balkans and Turkey.

The general winds between the western ridge and eastern low establish a meridional flow pattern, delivering a cold air mass across most of Eastern Europe and the Balkan Peninsula.

At the surface, the high-pressure area linked to the strong blocking high over the west will rapidly expand into Scandinavia and Central Europe as cold waves emerge across Eastern Europe.

This will allow meridional flow to spread across Eastern Europe, including eastern portions of Central Europe and the whole Balkan Peninsula.

On Tuesday, a widespread cold air mass spread across the Balkan Peninsula, reaching Greece and the Aegean Sea on Wednesday before it spread into the Black Sea region and the rest of Turkey on Wednesday and Thursday.

Temperatures in the lowest and mid-levels will be about 6-10 °C below normal for late September, which is pretty significant after the recent persistent warm periods. Europe will be split in two halves, as a ridge with higher-than-normal temperatures remains in the west.

Surface temperatures across the Balkans will be lowest on Tuesday, reaching 10-15 °C below long-term averages across Serbia, Bosnia, Romania and Bulgaria. Cold will also be significant for Greece and northwestern Turkey on Tuesday.

The dense Arctic air mass will continue further south and east towards Wednesday.

On Wednesday, the temperatures will be the most anomalous for Bulgaria, Greece and especially Turkey, with 12-16 °C colder than normal across Western Turkey.

With the core of the upper-level cold wave moving into the southern Balkans midweek, temperatures in its wake will gradually improve, with the ridge from Western Europe beginning to expand into Central Europe again late this week.

This week will bring dynamic but rapid displacement of warm continental air away from Eastern and partly Central Europe, thanks to the Arctic intrusion. The sharp temperature drop will follow behind the polar front after Tuesday.

Nighttime lows will plummet as the air mass clears behind the polar cold front, pushing Tuesday and Wednesday mornings into the low single digits. This could locally deliver freezing levels and the first frosts of the autumn season 2026.

It will also cool during the day. First, cold winds will bring a cold Tuesday, followed by a cold Wednesday as the core of the polar low remains over the south-central Balkans and Western Turkey.

Temperatures will remain in the upper 10s to low 20s across the south-central Balkans, well below normal for this time of year. The touristic season is still in full swing in Greece and Turkey.

We will continue to monitor the weather pattern and update the forecasts accordingly. Long-term trends suggest the European pattern will remain as a dipole until late this week, then the upper-level ridge will expand into Central and Eastern Europe as the end of September nears. Stay tuned for updates.

WetterZentrale and WXcharts provided images used in this article.

title: Many Choices Lie Ahead
description: Jonny Evans, Reader at the University of Lancaster I don’t use LLMS. I’m not going to say that you shouldn’t; it’s a choice. I don’t see the advent of LLMs as an exist…
fullText:
Jonny Evans, Reader at the University of Lancaster

I don’t use LLMS. I’m not going to say that you shouldn’t; it’s a choice.

I don’t see the advent of LLMs as an existential challenge to mathematicians. Why would we lose our fascination with deep truths, patterns and connections just because computers can help? That, too, is a choice.

I am continually surprised and disappointed to hear eminent mathematicians speculating on the end of mathematics and on the idea that there would be nothing left for us to do. No matter how powerful the technology becomes, how could that be true? If a theorem gets proved in a forest when nobody is there to hear it, what difference would it make to human understanding? These new things are tools, which humans can choose to use to help them do maths. If a senior mathematician is openly speculating that maths is a dead subject, all they are doing is driving away the young proto-mathematicians who would otherwise be pushing and developing the subject in 20-30 years’ time.

The reason it looks to some as if the end is nigh is that a lot of energy and capital is currently being expended by big companies to produce impressive theorems, independently of the mathematical professoriate, and they are succeeding: I was genuinely interested by the existence of a complex structure on the 6-sphere. Of course, they are doing this to prove to their investors that they have achieved something and that more investment would be welcomed. But if there were no human mathematicians to gawp and tell them how significant are their results, the investors wouldn’t be much impressed. This is the reason for my firm conviction that attempts by mathematicians to provide said companies with benchmarks or open problems to test out their machines are misguided, though I understand they come from well-intentioned efforts to hold these companies accountable to science. The truth is that these companies are accountable only to their investors, and science is a secondary concern.

The biggest existential risk to mathematics is what it has always been: a widespread public belief that mathematics is all solved and what’s the point of it anyway? Whilst the advent of LLMs re-unearths both of these questions, they are much older than LLMs. Of course, we know that maths will never be “all solved” by any finite state automaton (like a human or a computer). Any progress is just pushing back against the infinite cloud of unknowing. The question “what’s the point?” is much more apposite, and should be at the forefront of our minds more often than it is.

If we think maths is a race to prove theorems, the harder the better, then what is the point? Take a paragon of a result like Fermat’s Last Theorem: does it help anyone to know that there are no solutions to an+bn=cna^n + b^n = c^n? No, and that’s not the point. Indeed, if an LLM found a counterexample tomorrow, nothing would really change except the stress levels of the global population of number theorists. The problem inspired centuries of mathematical development before it was finally resolved. Whole swathes of algebraic number theory were developed by people frustrated by the fact they couldn’t answer this one, highly specific and ultimately pointless question about triples of integers. The result was a thriving discipline, having deep and surprising connections and interactions with other areas like cryptography. By the time the result was proved, it had served its purpose: mathematics was a richer field which touched the world in more ways. The fact that we now know the answer to the original problem is not the point.

Mathematics, like astronomy, literature, or history, is about helping human understanding to flourish. Of course, LLMs, used well, could help with that. However, these companies are pushing the narrative that maths is a race to prove big-name conjectures, because they believe their technology can excel at that. This is precisely the kind of activity which, seen from the outside, looks wholly pointless. They’re helped in this by the fact that many mathematicians have pushed the same narrative, because that’s how they have motivated themselves to make progress and measured the progress we have made. The whole system of rewards: top journals, top prizes, is dominated by this worldview. No wonder that at the top of mathematics, we find those who are now wondering loudly about the demise of mathematics, or even abandoning the subject themselves.

Whether or not we use the tools they produce, we cannot let these companies, whose interests are orthogonal to our own, dictate how we practice our subject. Letting them do so is a choice. It’s the choice to make promotional videos for AI companies. It’s the choice to hand over your favourite problems to them in exchange for temporary free access to a “frontier model” and then blog breathlessly about the results. It’s the choice to push for institutional subscriptions, when the time comes. It’s the choice to give a sense of inevitabilism and defeat, or pressure and anxiety when you talk to the early career researchers in your department. It’s the choice to say, when they knock down your favourite Clay Problem or Named Hypothesis, that you are now redundant.

Whether or not you use their tools, you can choose not to do any of these things. You can choose to promote a healthy vision for what mathematics will be and should always have been. You can choose how you contribute to the flourishing of human understanding. You can choose to be a mathematician.

title: 'Epigenetic' editing banishes hepatitis B virus
description: Technique uses chemical tags to shut down viral DNA lurking in host’s genome.
fullText:
A wave of epigenetic therapies is offering hope as ways to cure chronic hepatitis B — a lingering liver infection that is caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV) and affects more than 250 million people around the world. Currently available drugs often fail to eradicate the virus from the body.

Gene-editing therapies — which make cuts to the DNA strands — have been explored but for hepatitis B, they can increase cancer risks. Researchers are turning instead to epigenetic editing, which modifies markers attached to the DNA to alter how genes are turned on and off.

Scientists working at the biotechnology firm nChroma Bio in Boston, Massachusetts, and at institutes in Milan, Italy, have now placed chemical tags onto the HBV genome to shut down its gene activity and prevent it from producing viral particles. They achieved promising results in experiments on human liver cells and in mice, and the therapy generated only minimal and temporary side effects when tested in monkeys. The study was published in Nature Biomedical Engineering on 21 September1.

The efficacy of a single injection was “quite impressive”. This “is really where we need to go to end up being able to address this pandemic of HBV around the world”, says John Tavis, a molecular virologist at Saint Louis University in Missouri.

The preclinical findings “supported clinical advancement of this approach”, says study co-author Angelo Lombardo, a molecular biologist at the San Raffaele Telethon Institute for Gene Therapy in Milan, Italy. nChroma Bio has now launched a clinical trial to test multiple doses of the treatment in Hong Kong and New Zealand. The first participant received the therapy, through an intravenous infusion, in January.

The trial in humans is “a huge step” and “a realization of many, many years of work”, adds Lombardo, who co-founded nChroma Bio but does not have an official role at the firm. nChroma Bio declined Nature’s request to comment on the study.

HBV infections can turn into life-long challenges because the virus has ways to remain in the body and trick the immune system into not fighting against it. One of these is making free-ranging mini-chromosomes that can hide inside liver cells for a very long time.

These twists of viral DNA form “a genomic archive of the virus”, which help it to replicate when people stop taking anti-HBV drugs and lead to a severe rebound of the disease, explains virologist and clinical hepatologist Fabien Zoulim at the University of Lyon in France. Less than 10% of people who are treated for HBV for at least 10 years can cease their daily medications without such risk, Zoulim adds.

HBV can also stitch pieces of its genome into its host’s DNA and generate proteins that alter the immune response against it. The integration of viral DNA causes molecular changes in liver cells that can lead to cancer, Zoulim says.

nChroma’s therapy — named CRMA-1001 — contains a version of CRISPR’s Cas9 enzyme that lacks its normal enzymatic cutting activity. It also features RNA strands that lead the enzyme to its specific target in the HBV genome.

Encapsulated in a lipid nanoparticle, the therapy pulls a double duty to silence both free-ranging and integrated HBV DNAs by tagging them with methyl groups.

title: Google CC, an AI agent built for families
description: Google Labs is expanding CC to groups, starting with families and households, so they can spend less time on logistics.
fullText:
Google Labs introduces a new experimental agent built for families, helping households spend less time on logistics and more time together.

Senior Product Manager, Google Labs

When we launched CC, our goal was to build a personal agent that helps you get ahead of your day. It quickly became a daily habit for many early testers and in May we brought it to the Gemini App as Daily Brief.

One of our top user requests was for CC to do more to help run a busy home. Between school schedules, sports practices, paying bills, and figuring out what’s for dinner, managing a household is often a shared responsibility with a lot of coordination, made even more challenging with information spread over multiple user accounts.

Today, CC is becoming an agent for families and households. It has its own Google account that gives CC a distinct identity and clear permissions model, enabling up to six members to manage and collaborate with the agent. CC only sees what each member chooses to share, such as emails from your child’s school, the local swim center, or the vet. It automatically sorts through them and creates a shared daily brief and connects to Calendar and Tasks, helping families spend less time coordinating logistics and more time just being together.

With shared context in one place, CC helps keep daily routines for groups such as families and households running smoothly:

Add family members to your CC and pull in relevant information for Your Day Ahead brief, delivered right to your inbox.

CC can automatically add calendar events based on what your family shares.

CC can take action, like filling out forms, with your permission.

Easily control what you share with CC.

CC is an early experiment from Google Labs, available on web and mobile for people (18+) in the U.S with a personal Google account. Existing users will receive an email in the coming days to upgrade their account and new users can join the waitlist.

title: A Self-hosted Deferred Deep linking. Firebase dynamic link model
description: Self-hosted deferred deep linking and referral attribution for React Native. An open-source replacement for the deferred-linking half of Firebase Dynamic Links — Android Install Referrer, iOS clipb...
fullText:
A deferred deep linking referral system you fork and self-host: four
packages — two interchangeable backends, plus web and mobile — and runnable
examples. In production at Sparkle, a Nigerian
microfinance bank. New here? Read this file top to bottom — it's
written as a guided path, not a reference dump: what this is, how it works,
how to run it, and where to go next depending on what you're trying to do.

A referral link tapped on a real iPhone, on cellular, installing from the
App Store — and the code arriving in the signup field on the other side.
This isn't the demo app or a staged build: it's
Sparkle's live production release, a Nigerian
microfinance bank, running this SDK.

Thirty-five seconds, one take, nothing sped up or cut:

That half-second is the entire point of the iOS deterministic tier. The
code was written to the clipboard by the landing page moments before the
App Store redirect, survived the install, and came back without a network
call, a fingerprint guess, or the user typing anything.

Two details worth watching for, because both are deliberate:

This is the iOS path, which is the harder one to believe — it depends on a
clipboard payload surviving Safari, the App Store and an install. Android
is the easy case and needs no video: the Play Install Referrer hands the
code over before the app's first frame.

Want to drive it yourself rather than watch? Quick start
has a live web demo and an Android APK.

Deterministic and probabilistic recovery are two separate mechanisms, not
two branches of one path — shown below as two diagrams, both starting at
the same click and ending at the same claim.

Android's default path, and iOS's opt-in path — both read a code and proof
entirely on-device, no network call. Neither touches fingerprint matching
at all.

Reached only when the deterministic path above didn't run or didn't have
anything to read — a scored guess, backed by the same signed token once it
succeeds. Both platforms feed the same scoring engine; this is the one
piece of matching logic that isn't platform-specific at all.

Reliability: Android deterministic recovery hits ~100% of real
installs; iOS deterministic recovery depends entirely on whether the paste
button is rendered and tapped. Probabilistic matching sees an observed
~85–90% match rate on iOS, where it's the default fallback; lower priority
on Android, where it's a fallback of last resort.

Treat that iOS figure as what a single self-hosted deployment sees, and
don't compare it directly against a commercial MMP's published numbers.
Branch and AppsFlyer score probabilistic matches against signal pooled
across their whole SDK install base — many apps, shared IP graphs — while
this only ever sees your own clicks. That's a structural difference in
available signal, not a tuning gap you can close by adjusting weights.

The proof that makes both deterministic paths possible: every
recovered code carries a signed proof (click_id.expiry.hmac), minted
once at /click — this is what lets both deterministic paths stay
genuinely network-free at recovery time, and what /claim verifies before
any reward is paid out. A code with no valid token behind it (including
one a user typed in by hand) can reach signup, but can never clear
/claim — see docs/decisions.md #21/#22 for the
full reasoning behind why this replaced an earlier redeem-round-trip
design.

Read the scope line first, because it's the part that decides whether
this is for you: Branch and AppsFlyer are mobile measurement platforms.
blynk-deferlink is the deferred-deep-linking and referral-attribution
slice of what they do, self-hosted. If you need ad-network attribution,
this is not a replacement.

Worth being blunt about, because it's most of what the money buys:

When to use them instead: you're running paid acquisition and need
MMP attribution; you want fraud protection you don't have to build; or
you'd rather buy a supported product than operate one. Those are good
reasons, and this project doesn't pretend otherwise.

When to use this: referral and invite flows are the attribution you
care about, you want the data in your own database, or a per-MAU bill
doesn't make sense for your margins.

FDL was deprecated in May 2023 with no official replacement and shut
down completely on 25 August 2025 — every link stopped resolving,
deferred linking included. If that's what brought you here, this is
probably a closer fit than Branch is.

FDL was never an MMP. It did link hosting, Universal/App Links handling,
deferred deep linking, and basic click analytics — and nothing else. No
ad-network attribution, no fraud detection, no campaign analytics. So the
honest mapping is:

In other words: this covers the deferred-attribution half of FDL, not
the link-hosting half. That's the honest scope. If all you needed was the
deferred part — which for referral flows is usually the case — the gap is
smaller than it looks, and you get to keep the data.

Running in production at Sparkle, a Nigerian
microfinance bank, on the PHP backend — real referral traffic, real
conversions. A second Sparkle app is rolling out on it now. The Node
backend serves this project's own live demo.

See it live in production: https://sparkle.ng/referral/L82WDL — a real
Sparkle referral link, served by this SDK. Open it on a phone to watch the
actual flow: the landing page registers a click, hands the code off, and
the app recovers it after install. (It's the maintainer's own referral
link — Sparkle only credits a referral once a referred user completes a
first transaction, so opening it to watch the mechanics does nothing. It's
here because a real production link demonstrates more than a staged one.)

One thing worth knowing: coverage is uneven by package. The scoring
engine, click tokens and conversion tracking are well covered on both
backends; referral-web's test suite is new and still thin. CI runs every
suite on each PR across both Node and PHP version ranges.

docs/decisions.md is the honest record of how this was built — including
the bugs found by actually running it on real devices, and the trade-offs
accepted rather than solved. It's the fastest way to judge whether the
engineering here meets your bar.

Don't want to clone anything yet? Try the recovery flow live
— pick a referral code and it builds a real link to the actual production
landing page (real countdown, real click registration, real clipboard
handoff), then recovers it exactly how a real installed app would (Android:
automatic via the Play referrer param; iOS: a real clipboard check, falling
back to a real fingerprint match), with the actual request/response for
every step.

Want the real mobile app, not just the web half? Download the Android
demo APK
— open that link on an Android device and install it; no Play Store
listing and no Expo account needed. You'll have to allow installs from
your browser the first time, since it's unlisted rather than
Play-distributed. It's served from a GitHub
release
deliberately: the EAS build link this used to point at expires after 30
days, and did — a release asset doesn't. iOS has no equivalent link —
internal distribution there needs a registered Apple Developer account and
per-device UDID registration, so for now the iOS side is only reachable by
building it yourself (see below), or by watching it run in production in
See it working above.

Otherwise, the fastest way to see the whole thing work locally, before
installing anything for real. Three terminals. No PHP or database required
— the mock backend covers it.

Open the web page with ?code=1234 and watch the backend log the click. On
desktop it shows both store buttons; on a phone browser it attempts the app
handoff then redirects to the store.

The mobile app recovers automatically on launch, same as a real app —
there's nothing to simulate inside it. To see it actually find something,
type a code into its own "Generate a referral link" card and tap Open
link — that opens the real landing page in your device/simulator's
browser (real countdown, real click registration, real clipboard handoff),
then switch back to the app to see the recovery.

Once the demo makes sense, this is where to go depending on what you're
actually trying to do:

Setting this up for real — pick the piece you need:

The four recovery paths (deterministic/probabilistic × Android/iOS),
diagrammed, live in How it works above rather than a
separate doc — it's central enough to the project to read before anything
else, not something to click away for.

Understanding why it's built this way, not just how to use it:
docs/decisions.md — the engineering-decisions log.
Every non-obvious choice in this codebase (why matching uses a graduated
recency score, why /claim requires a signed token instead of trusting the
request, why the mobile SDK persists nothing to disk) is written up there
with the problem it solved, in chronological order.

API/config reference for a package you've already set up lives in that
package's own README (packages/*/README.md) — the integration guides above
are the walkthrough; the READMEs are what to come back to for a specific
config field or endpoint shape.

Fork it and run it as your own. That's the intended model, not a
temporary state of affairs. Attribution data is the thing you least want
sitting behind someone else's API: every click, every device fingerprint,
every conversion. Self-hosting means the click table lives in your
database, the matching runs on your server, and nobody can reprice,
rate-limit, sunset, or read it. Firebase Dynamic Links shut down in August
2025 and took every link with it; that risk is the whole reason this
exists, and shipping it as a hosted dependency would just recreate it.

So there's no registry install. Fork or clone, point the backend at your
database, and change whatever doesn't fit — the code is yours at that
point, and the API contract is small enough to modify without fear (two
independent backends implement it, which is the proof it's not tangled).

The full reasoning, including what this costs you — slower to adopt than
npm install, and forks get no automatic security updates — is
decision #31.

This is how it runs in production today. Sparkle, a
Nigerian microfinance bank, runs its referral programme on it: the PHP
backend SDK deployed on their own infrastructure, against their own
database and their own reward logic. Nothing in this repo is a staging
copy of that — it's the same code path, which is why the bugs in
docs/decisions.md were found on real devices rather
than in tests.

The packages are consumed from source. Three ways, depending on how your
project is laid out:

1. Workspaces (what this repo uses). From the repo root:

The examples already declare the SDKs as file: dependencies, so they resolve
to the local source automatically.

2. A file: dependency in your own project.

React Native's Metro bundles the SDK straight from its TypeScript source (the
package's react-native field points at src/), so no build step is needed for
the mobile SDK. The web SDK is consumed from source here via a Vite alias; for a
non-source consumer, build it first (below).

3. A tarball. Build, pack, then install the .tgz anywhere:

Publishing your fork privately. If your team would rather consume these
as ordinary dependencies than as source, publish them to your own registry
under your own scope: npm run build:sdks, then npm publish in each
package, and composer / Packagist for the PHP one. Renaming the scope in
each package.json is the only change required.

Contributions are genuinely welcome, and the project is set up so that a
first one is easy to land.

CONTRIBUTING.md covers setup, how to run each
package's tests, and what to verify before opening a PR. CI runs every
suite on each PR across both Node and PHP version ranges, so you get
automated feedback without waiting on a review.

Good first issues are labelled
good first issue

title: Synthesia Interactive Avatar API
description: Developers can now embed a real-time, photorealistic, lip-synced interactive avatar or our brand new Style Avatars powered by our latest Express-3 model into their web product via our API.
fullText:
Create AI videos with 240+ avatars in 160+ languages

Gartner forecasts that by 2028, seven in 10 customer journeys will begin with a conversational third-party interface. Until now, embedding a real-time, photorealistic interactive avatar into a website or app meant choosing between closed-stack vendors which offered limited customization and vendor lock-in or hand-stitched integrations with high latency and poor reliability.

Today, we’re launching the Synthesia Interactive Avatar API to shift from broadcast video to actual conversation: real-time, interruptible, personalized, and agentic. Our Avatars can respond in any language and in real-time, and will soon be able to take actions such as scheduling follow-up meetings.

Enterprise customers are already shipping Interactive Avatars in production, from HR onboarding and customer service to in-person kiosk experiences. You can experience it yourself by talking to Synthesia’s own press officer here.

Synthesia is taking a Bring-Your-Own-Stack (BYO) approach to Interactive Avatars, enabling customers to supply their own LLM, speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers while Synthesia handles the real-time, lip-synced avatar rendering.

1. Bring your own AI stack, by default. Connect your own LLM from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or any other provider, STT (any provider), and optionally TTS. Synthesia layers the avatar on top via LiveKit, and we also offer a Synthesia-hosted TTS inside the plugin as an add-on.

2. Real-time, streaming lip sync that feels natural. The avatar responds with idle and listening behaviour, so conversations flow smoothly even during pauses. Interruptions and turn-taking work out of the box. Customers can build completely customizable avatars from photorealistic to branded characters like an animated mascot, with custom backgrounds.

‍3. Language-agnostic and customizable. Lip sync works with a number of languages including French, German or Spanish, as well as accents. Use stock synthetic avatars or create custom ones, including branded Style Avatars from Avatar Builder, and make them interactive via API.

Here is technology stack needed to build an interactive video experience:

Owning the conversation layer gives customers control over data, guardrails and system prompts. Today’s release also unlocks agentic functions, so an avatar can book meetings, complete a form or trigger a workflow mid-conversation rather than just respond to it.

We’ve built this for teams that ship production-ready AI experiences, not demos:

Interactive Avatar runs on the same platform businesses already trust for their video, offering enterprise-grade security (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001), systems management (ISO 42001), data privacy (GDPR and CCPA compliance), and workspace controls (SSO and SCIM). Because you bring your own AI, your data governance model doesn't change: the Avatar never sees your knowledge base, and your model never leaves your infrastructure.

Interactive Avatars are available now for Enterprise customers. The full-stack pipeline (Synthesia-hosted LLM + TTS + avatar, no code needed) will launch on October 1, 2026, for teams who prefer a managed approach.

Try it out here: https://www.synthesia.io/features/avatars/interactive-avatars

Alessandra Venier is a Corporate Affairs Manager at Synthesia

Building the Global AI Video Platform for Business: Why Synthesia is Expanding in the U.S.

We've opened our new US headquarters in New York City: 50,000 square feet in Manhattan's Flatiron District, nearly four times the size of our previous space. With around half of our revenue now coming from the US, we're investing where our customers are.

Synthesia Launches New AI Assistant for Faster Video Creation and Express-3 Avatar Model

Today, we’re launching Assistant, the easiest way to go from an idea to an on-brand video with one prompt, and Express-3, our most lifelike avatar model yet, which also powers our brand new Style Avatars. With our new Assistant, you describe what you want and Synthesia structures the video, plans it with you, builds it on-brand, and lets you refine it, all in one text-based chat without hopping between tools. For the first time, the entire video creation workflow lives in one place.

Say Hello to Synthesia's New AI Press Officer

Today, we're introducing an AI press officer to our Newsroom: an Interactive Avatar built with the voice and likeness of Alexandru Voica, our global head of corporate affairs. Ask it a question about Synthesia and it answers in a live conversation, the same way you would talk to a member of our corporate affairs team.
