title: Vermont man convicted of attempted murder in shooting of 3 Palestinian college students
description:
Burlington, Vt. (AP) — A jury on Monday convicted a Vermont man of attempted murder in the shootings of three Palestinian college students who were walking near his home, rejecting an insanity defense rooted in his claims that he was acting on orders from U.S. and Israeli intelligence agencies.
Jason Eaton faces up to life in prison in the November 2023 attack in Burlington, which paralyzed Hisham Awartani from the waist down and wounded his friends, Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid.
fullText:
Burlington, Vt. (AP) — A jury on Monday convicted a Vermont man of attempted murder in the shootings of three Palestinian college students who were walking near his home, rejecting an insanity defense rooted in his claims that he was acting on orders from U.S. and Israeli intelligence agencies.

Jason Eaton faces up to life in prison in the November 2023 attack in Burlington, which paralyzed Hisham Awartani from the waist down and wounded his friends, Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid.

The men, all 20 at the time, had been visiting Awartani's grandmother for Thanksgiving. They were smoking cigarettes and speaking a mix of English and Arabic as they walked near the University of Vermont campus after dusk. Two of them were wearing traditional Palestinian scarves known as keffiyehs.

The jury deliberated for several hours before reaching its verdict after a weeklong trial that saw testimony from the three men, who recounted how their stroll ended in bloodshed, and defense and prosecution psychiatric experts who offered differing views of Eaton's mental health and criminal culpability.

Eaton, 51, stared ahead blankly as the verdict was read, standing alongside his lawyers — public defenders whom he tried to fire last week over his concerns that his defense hadn't been "adequately presented." Judge John Pacht, who blocked Eaton's midtrial bid to act as his own lawyer, ordered him jailed pending sentencing, which has yet to be scheduled.

Awartani and Aliahmad watched from the front row of the courtroom gallery, smiling and hugging people around them.

"The verdict cannot undo what happened or erase the trauma our families still carry, but it affirms something fundamental: Jason Eaton is responsible for what he did," Awartani's mother, Elizabeth Price, told reporters afterward.

Eaton had pleaded not guilty but did not dispute that he was the shooter. He claimed that the CIA and Mossad transmitted their orders via FM radio and that God was commanding him to protect his Jewish neighbors. His lawyers had urged jurors to find him not guilty by reason of insanity, an outcome that would've spared him from prison but could have required that he undergo mental health treatment.

Eaton's lawyers, Margaret Jansch and Joshua O'Hara, said he had struggled with mental health issues his whole life, including diagnoses of attention deficit, post-traumatic stress, bipolar, depression and borderline personality disorders, culminating in a psychotic break after losing his job at a credit union two weeks before the shooting.

Prosecutor Sarah George countered that Eaton was a narcissist but not legally insane. He had a grandiose sense of self-importance and lacked empathy but was fully aware of the criminality of his conduct, George said in a closing argument. He appeared nervous when police arrived at his door, repeatedly asked for a lawyer and hasn't claimed to have received any other messages directing his actions, she said.

Eaton told officers that he had a shotgun in his apartment, but didn't disclose that he had other weapons, including a Ruger .380-caliber handgun that was found in a bedroom dresser and that crime lab testing concluded was used in the shooting, said George, the Chittenden County state's attorney.

The shooting, weeks after the start of the Israel-Hamas war, shook Burlington, and reverberated in the West Bank, where the three wounded men grew up and became friends as schoolmates in Ramallah before moving to the U.S. for college. It spawned calls for a hate crime investigation.

But no hate crime charges were filed as questions persisted about whether anti-Palestinian animus, an altered mental state or something else had compelled Eaton to open fire. After the verdict, Awartani's mother said Eaton's hateful rhetoric, aired at the trial, had made it clear why he targeted her son.

Days after the shooting, George said in her closing argument, Eaton had told his lawyers that he wished Awartani's grandmother had warned him that the men were "going to dress up like terrorists" and trek through his neighborhood.

"Or see, if grandma had said to them, you know, maybe now's not a great time to wear that thing on your head," George said, paraphrasing Eaton's remarks. "You know, things are a little tense when you've got American hostages over in Palestine, and we're trying to get them back."

"They were not the words of a man confused about who he shot or why," Elizabeth Price said. "They were the words a man who saw three young men speaking the language of their childhood and wearing what made them feel closer to their far away families and homes and decided to kill them because of his own prejudices."

Awartani testified last week that he first noticed Eaton standing on a porch as they approached the apartment house where he lived. Within seconds, Awartani said, Eaton was off the porch and walking toward them. His face was expressionless and he didn't say anything. As Eaton got to about 5 to 10 feet (1.5 to 3 meters) away, "he pulled out a handgun and started shooting at us," Awartani said.

Abdalhamid, a student at Haverford College near Philadelphia, said he fled and hid behind another home after seeing Aliahmad fall to the ground. He said he only realized later when he sat down that he had also been wounded.

Awartani, who was studying at Brown University in Rhode Island at the time, was shot in the chest and the bullet ricocheted off his scapula, causing paraplegia in his spinal cord. Aliahmad, who was a student at Trinity College in Connecticut, was struck in the collarbone, and Abdalhamid was shot in the right buttock.

Jacob Pyne, who lived in a different apartment in the same house as Eaton, testified that he heard four to six gunshots, followed by footsteps going up the stairs of the apartment house. He said he ran outside and heard two men speaking, one of whom was more vocal and yelling, "I've been shot, help me." He then brought the men blankets and called 911.

Eaton didn't testify. In an opening statement last week, O'Hara told jurors that Eaton claimed he started receiving messages while listening to a local NPR affiliate. At first, the messages were encouraging and validating, the lawyer said, but subsequent messages turned dark, insisting that Eaton "has to go out and shoot somebody."

title: The 2026 midterms are 6 weeks away. What the latest polls say.
description:
The 2026 midterm elections are just 43 days away. All of the key primaries have been decided. With summer officially behind us, the fall campaign is now underway.
So where do things stand — nationwide — in the race to control Congress? Which party has a better chance of, you know, winning?
fullText:
The 2026 midterm elections are just 43 days away. All of the key primaries have been decided. With summer officially behind us, the fall campaign is now underway.

So where do things stand — nationwide — in the race to control Congress? Which party has a better chance of, you know, winning? To get a sense of that, it helps to zoom out … and geek out over some cold, hard data.

The usual caveats apply, of course. Polls aren't predictions; they're momentary snapshots of public opinion. Big events can, and often do, change the course of elections. And six weeks can be an eternity in politics.

Yet the stakes in November couldn't be higher, especially for President Trump, who has enjoyed complete Republican control of Congress for the first half of his second term. Flipping the House would give Democrats the power to block the president's agenda, investigate his administration and even impeach him (again); flipping the Senate would allow them to stymie his Supreme Court nominees too.

The state-by-state midterm landscape is finally taking shape — and a few clear polling trends are emerging. Here are the numbers to watch as Election Day nears.

Every pollster asks a version of the same question: If an election for U.S. Congress were held today, which party's candidate would you vote for in your district? In fact, this particular polling prompt is so pervasive, it's known as the "generic ballot" (at least among politics nerds).

You obviously can't divine the outcome of an entire midterm election from a single question that flattens 435 House contests into a binary choice between "the Democrat" and "the Republican." But the generic ballot can suggest which direction voters are heading.

History is helpful here, courtesy of the RealClear Politics polling average:

At this point in 2022 — after more than a year and a half of Democratic President Joe Biden and Democratic majorities in the House and Senate — Democrats had a narrow lead (1.3 percentage points) on the generic ballot. Six weeks later, the GOP translated its final polling lead of 3 percentage points into nine seats — enough to flip the House.

At this point in 2018 — with Trump as president and Republican majorities in the House and Senate — Democrats were leading by an average of 8 points on the generic ballot. Six weeks later, they picked up 41 seats and flipped the House.

Polarization wasn't as extreme in 2014 and 2010, the two midterms under Democratic President Barack Obama; minds weren't made up quite so early. But six weeks out, voters were starting to break against Democrats. In 2014, a final Republican polling lead of 2.4 points translated into a net gain of 13 seats in the House; in 2010, those numbers were 9.4 points and 63 seats, respectively.

So what does that mean for 2026? Historically speaking, a president's party almost always loses seats when voters return to the polls to judge his first two years in office. Sometimes, the backlash is so pervasive that the president's party loses pretty much every close-ish contest — a phenomenon known as a "wave" election.

Right now, Democrats have a wave-sized lead on the generic ballot — about 8 percentage points, on average — and it has been steadily growing over the last two weeks.

Democrats probably won't reprise 2018 and flip 41 House seats again in November, in part because red-state Republican lawmakers have recently redrawn congressional maps across the South to benefit their party in ways that blue-state Democrats have been unable to keep up with. But they only need to pick up three seats to win back the House.

National dynamics tend to define the composition of the incoming House. But Senate contests are quirkier — more state-specific and personality-driven. Democrats currently hold 47 Senate seats; they'd need 51 to control the chamber. (A 50-50 split would give Vice President JD Vance the tiebreaking vote). Polls suggest that flipping four Republican seats is possible — but Dems are also playing defense in places like Michigan, Georgia and New Hampshire. Here are the 10 races to follow:

Republican Susan Collins (incumbent)

What the latest polls say: Jackson, who replaced Graham Platner, the Democrats' previous scandal-plagued nominee, tends to lead Collins by anywhere from 2 to 8 percentage points. One recent poll shows a tie.

Republican Mike Rogers (former member of Congress)

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed (public-health epidemiologist and former Wayne County, Mich. health director)

What the latest polls say: Eight polls have been conducted over the last month. Seven of them showed El-Sayed in the lead, by anywhere from 2 to 5 percentage points.

Republican Jon Husted (incumbent)

Democrat Sherrod Brown (former senator)

What the latest polls say: Every poll conducted since July shows Brown leading Husted, with margins ranging from 4 to 8 percentage points.

Democrat Jon Ossoff (incumbent)

Republican Mike Collins (member of Congress)

What the latest polls say: Ossoff holds a solid lead over Collins, with the two most recent polls putting him ahead by 4 to 7 percentage points.

Republican Michael Whatley (former Republican National Committee chairman)

Democrat Roy Cooper (former governor)

What the latest polls say: Cooper leads by more than 8 points, on average. One poll conducted in Septemeber showed him ahead by 15.

Republican John E. Sununu (former U.S. senator)

Democrat Chris Pappas (four-term U.S. representative) 

What the latest polls say: Pappas and Sununu, who both won their Sept. 8 primaries, have traded leads in recent polls in the race to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. But the most recent survey, conducted from Sept. 16 to 17, showed Pappas ahead by 8.

Republican Dan Sullivan (incumbent)

Democrat Mary Peltola (former member of Congress)

What the latest polls say: Most surveys conducted since Alaska's Aug. 18 primary have given Peltola a slim lead; a mid-September AARP poll showed her ahead by 7. But the most recent sounding suggests this could be a photo finish.

Republican Ashley Hinson (member of Congress)

Democrat Josh Turek (state legislator and former Paralympic athlete)

What the latest polls say: Hinson and Turek have traded small leads in surveys released since Iowa's June 2 primaries.

Republican Ken Paxton (state attorney general)

Democrat James Talarico (state legislator)

What the latest polls say: Nearly every poll conducted over the summer has shown Talarico leading Paxton, though the margins are small — between 1 and 6 points.

Republican Pete Ricketts (incumbent and former governor)

Independent Dan Osborn (veteran and former union leader with Democratic support)

What the latest polls say: Surveys are few and far between. But the most recent results suggest Osborn could be competitive.

Advantage? Too close to call — though Democrats seem to have gained ground over the last two weeks.

To one degree or another, midterm elections are always referendums on how the president is performing. So Trump is the final piece of the puzzle.

At the moment, that's unfortunate news for Republicans on Capitol Hill and those looking to join them.

According to the data journalists at Silver Bulletin, 59% of Americans, on average, currently disapprove of how Trump is handling his job vs. 39% who approve. That puts the president's net disapproval rating at 20%.

An American Research Group poll released on Monday measured Trump's approval rating at 29% — his lowest mark ever. The same survey showed the president's disapproval rating at 68%.

Again, history can provide perspective. In mid-September 2018, Trump was about 12 points "underwater"; Republicans went on to lose 41 seats that November.

Trump is earning even lower marks on voters' top 2026 issue: the cost of living. Shortly after he returned to office, roughly equal numbers of Americans approved and disapproved of how the president was handling inflation. But today, 71% disapprove and 26% approve. That's a 45-point gap.

In comparison, Biden's approval rating on inflation was rarely underwater by more than 30 points during his presidency  — a period that coincided with the economic shocks of COVID-19 and ended with him choosing not to stand for reelection.

title: 5,000 delays reported after FAA issues ground stops at Northeast airports
description:
Flyers across the United States are facing massive disruptions to their travel plans on Monday after equipment outages stopped flights at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey and Philadelphia International Airport in Pennsylvania, with no estimated time for resuming service.
More than 900 flights have been canceled nationwide and over 5,000 are delayed on Monday, with Newark and Philadelphia hit the hardest.
The issues began when a circuit blew at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility Monday morning, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said. When the backup system went into place, officials discovered the backup line in New Jersey had been cut, Bedford said.
NJ Transit - PHOTO: At approximately 9:45 a.
fullText:
More than 900 flights have been canceled nationwide.

Flyers across the United States are facing massive disruptions to their travel plans on Monday after equipment outages stopped flights at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey and Philadelphia International Airport in Pennsylvania, with no estimated time for resuming service.

More than 900 flights have been canceled nationwide and over 5,000 are delayed on Monday, with Newark and Philadelphia hit the hardest.

The issues began when a circuit blew at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility Monday morning, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said. When the backup system went into place, officials discovered the backup line in New Jersey had been cut, Bedford said.

In order to change the circuit in Philadelphia, Bedford said the airspace in the Northeast would be closing for at least 30 minutes, and ground stops were expanded to include New York City's John F. Kennedy International Airport and LaGuardia Airport as part of the work.

Airspace has since reopened at JFK and LaGuardia, but officials said the fix to replace the circuit in Philadelphia has not worked, leaving operations still halted at Philadelphia and Newark's airports, with no time estimate for when they'll resume.

The outage caused a ripple effect across the Northeast and the U.S., diverting some flights and canceling and delaying others.

United Airlines, which has one of its hubs at Newark Airport, said Monday afternoon that it's "canceling the rest of the day's planned domestic mainline and United Express flights to and from Newark." United said it will "prioritize remaining international departures."

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

ABC News' Jason Volack contributed to this report.

title: Meta May Try to Repair Its Poor Privacy Reputation at 'Connect 2026'
description: Meta Connect 2026 is nearly here, and may bring new camera-free smart glasses.
fullText:
Meta Connect 2026 is right around the corner. Like other annual tech events, such as Made by Google or Apple's fall event, Connect is Meta's chance to showcase the hardware and AI tools it plans to launch over the next year. The company may have started as a single social media platform, but it now dominates or competes in multiple tech fields, including virtual reality headsets, LLMs, and, as of late, personal AI agents, thanks to the introduction of Muse AI. Here's what I'm expecting to see at Meta Connect 2026.

While the company will undoubtedly announce new AI developments this week, Meta Connect 2026 will likely also make headlines for its hardware division. Meta is well known (perhaps infamous) for its smart glasses, so it only makes sense that the company would make relevant announcements during a major tech event. But the most newsworthy moment of all might not be an "advancement," so much as a refinement.

As PCMag reports, Meta is planning to announce camera-free smart glasses at Connect 2026. These glasses, codenamed "Luna," would rely on an array of six microphones rather than cameras to power AI features. That way, you could still ask Meta AI questions or give commands to Muse AI, without the need for cameras to tap into the world around you.

Meta's most popular smart glasses currently come with embedded cameras, so why the change? It's probably not to offer users a "budget" smart glasses option. Instead, it's more likely that Meta is responding to growing backlash over its current camera-enabled smart glasses. It turns out that, as popular as these glasses are, a lot of people don't like the idea of being stealthily recorded anywhere they go. The problem was made worse by an underground industry of hackers aiming to disable the recording light on Meta smart glasses, making it even harder to know whether someone was sneakily filming you.

To its credit, Meta has already responded to these "critiques." The company reportedly patched the exploit hackers were taking advantage of, so users shouldn't be able to bypass the recording light any longer: If the LED is blocked, Meta smart glasses are now supposed to disable video recording. Introducing camera-free smart glasses may be another step in that direction, but that won't change the fact that camera-embedded smart glasses are still readily accessible and easy to miss in passing. While there are steps individuals can take to protect their privacy in the face of these cameras, it's really an uphill battle.

It's not just smart glasses giving Meta PR trouble. The company recently settled a massive lawsuit for nearly $18 billion, ending legal action from most of the states. The lawsuit alleged that Meta's platforms were harmful and addictive to children and teens, and in addition to financial compensation, Meta is now changing its rules for underage users on its platforms. That comes just ahead of the release of The Social Reckoning, a movie dramatizing Meta whistleblower Frances Haugen's revelations about the company in The Wall Street Journal's "The Facebook Files" investigation. Meta also recently backtracked on an Instagram feature that let anyone generate AI images from your public photos. Meta Connect 2026 could be a bit of a reset for Meta in a rather unforgiving environment.

Meta could also take the opportunity to announce its long-rumored "Phoenix" mixed reality "glasses." Why the quotes? If rumors are to be believed, this device will be more of a headset than Meta's current smart glasses offerings, employing a goggles-like design, or perhaps something that looks like a "bulky pair of glasses."

That said, the expectation is that Phoenix will be more portable and practical than Meta Quest, the company's VR headset. Phoenix may use an external "compute puck" to handle advanced processes, which would allow the headset to be lighter than it otherwise might be. All the while, it could run HorizonOS, the same operating system Meta Quest headsets run. You might get the best of both worlds: A high-quality mixed reality experience without the need for a bulky headset.

As much as Meta Connect will likely focus on hardware, AI will also probably take up much of the presentation. Expect more updates about Muse AI, the company's new AI agent that can perform tasks on your behalf—even if Meta simply takes the opportunity to promote the feature. Meta may also announce a new version of Llama, the company's flagship AI model, which hasn't been updated since April of 2025, though I haven't seen any rumors about this specifically.

Meta Connect 2026 spans two days: Sept. 23 and Sept. 24. The keynote itself, however, is on the first day: Wednesday, Sept. 23 at 4 p.m. PT (7 p.m. ET). You should be able to access the livestream from Meta Connect's official site, though the stream isn't accessible at this time. (Meta has an option to "register" for the livestream, but it seems designed to send you an alert when the livestream is available.)

title: Why Your 'HIIT' Workouts Are Full of Empty Promises
description: The original HIIT was supposed to a cheat code for cardio gains. Today's HIIT is nothing like it.
fullText:
High-intensity interval training, or HIIT, made headlines in the 2010s with one specific claim: that short bursts of hard work can give the same aerobic benefits as longer sessions of jogging or cycling. But the HIIT videos you can stream today have very little to do with the original model, and many of them aren’t worth your time.

Before we break down the difference, I want to make something clear: If you love doing videos labeled “HIIT,” and they’re part of an exercise routine that makes you genuinely happy, keep on doing them. I’m not trying to take away a thing that you love.

But if you’re doing them because you feel they’re the best way to achieve your goals, or because a trainer or influencer tells you that they’ll burn a ton of calories or build your booty, we need to sit down for a little intervention.

High-intensity interval training was born as a buzzword after exercise scientists noticed that people got better at the Wingate test every time they took it. The Wingate protocol calls for people to pedal a stationary bike all-out, at a high resistance, for a pukeworthy 30 seconds. Then you get to rest for four minutes, and do it again.

After further experiments, researchers figured out that the benefits they saw, including increased aerobic fitness, could be triggered by other rest/work combinations. The Tabata protocol, again done on a research-grade exercise bike (“cycle ergometer,” they call it) is 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest, repeated "seven to eight times" to achieve exhaustion in the original study—or about four minutes in total.

These are not workouts that people do for fun. Everyone I’ve seen recount the experience has said that it was complete agony. The scientists often note that people can rarely push themselves hard enough to replicate these protocols on their own. Workout classes and videos don't push you that hard, either. Peloton offers "Tabata" classes that ask you to do those four-minute blocks several times in the same workout, meaning you definitely didn't push yourself to exhaustion on the first one.

To create a more accessible version of HIIT, Martin Gibala, one of the researchers who popularized the concept of HIIT, worked to find a version of the protocol that normal humans could do on their own, and that wouldn’t leave them so pooped they were scared to come back. His conclusion: one minute work/one minute rest was the sweet spot, and you could do it while cycling, jogging, or doing other aerobic activities. Interval workouts boomed in popularity, using a variety of work/rest intervals.

Another accessible version of HIIT is the Norwegian 4x4, which uses four-minute intervals at a hard but not exhaustive effort, with three minutes' rest in between, repeated four times. This takes longer than the HIIT protocols I mention above—about 40 minutes for a complete workout—but it's been shown to be effective for cardio gains.

The term HIIT didn’t just get watered down; it mutated. When it began, HIIT was about getting more results in less time, so it built a reputation as being more efficient, maybe even superior to things like jogging. And since you don’t need a bike to do HIIT, trainers ran with that idea and started applying the term to literally anything they could think of. Bodyweight squats? Bicep curls? Sure, why not. As a result, these days HIIT means something more like “a workout video with a timer counting down in the corner.”

HIIT’s popularity had been building for years when COVID hit, and from there it exploded. If you’re a trainer or influencer trying to come up with something you can easily film, you’ll probably gravitate to no-equipment home workouts. And to make them sound exciting, you’ll call them HIIT.

I suspect the label “HIIT” on a bodyweight workout is supposed to translate as “good enough.” Yeah, you’re doing a few lunges in your living room, but the trainer wants you to think it’s just as good as anything you could get from a boutique studio or a full-featured gym. Maybe better. For any reason you might want to work out—burning calories

You can tell how far removed these workouts are from real HIIT by judging the promises they make. Are they saying they’ll improve your VO2max, which was one of the original benefits noted? They won’t—not usually. Let’s do a quick rundown:

Do they burn a lot of calories? Not necessarily, but it depends on the workout. The longer the workout and the more out of breath you are, the more calories you’re burning. The truth is, 20 minutes of “HIIT” often doesn’t burn any more than 20 minutes of medium-intensity exercise like jogging.

Do they burn more calories after the workout? In theory, your body keeps burning calories after a hard workout session. But there are two caveats: First, this is only significant when the workout is really intense. Second, after you do a hard workout, your body often wants to conserve calories for the rest of the day, so it all evens out while you’re lying on the couch. Even Gibala has said that afterburn is overstated.

Do they help you lose weight? Diet matters more to weight loss than the amount of exercise you do, much less the specific type. Exercise can help a little bit with the “calories burned” side of the equation (as long as it doesn’t make you hungrier, which it sometimes does), but now we’re back to the reality that HIIT workouts don’t offer any special advantage in burning calories.

Do they build muscle? Maybe a little, but they won’t get you the booty/arms/whatever of your dreams. You optimize muscle growth with strength training routines that ask you to lift heavy and then rest until you're recovered again—usually at least one minute, often longer. "HIIT" workouts that keep you moving the whole time, or that only have short rests, can build some muscle, but pretty soon you’ll be strong enough that the workout isn’t challenging your muscles enough to grow. You really do need to train increasingly heavy if you want to build muscle.

First, ask yourself why you’re doing the video. Do you want to increase your aerobic fitness? Then evaluate whether following the video actually gets you out of breath and allows adequate rest for you to do it again. Do you want to build muscle? Then evaluate whether the video actually challenges your muscles.

As I mentioned above, sometimes we do “HIIT” videos not for any specific outcome, but because it feels good to move our bodies and we like the moves in the video. This is fine and good, and it definitely counts toward the 75 to 150 minutes of exercise you should be getting weekly. But if you have specific goals, seek out the best ways to achieve them. Chances are, there’s something out there that’s better for you than yet another “HIIT” video.

title: Do This If You Want Another Year of Windows 10 Security Updates
description: ESU coverage for Windows 10 is being extended through October 2027.
fullText:
If you are still holding on to Windows 10, there's good news: Microsoft is offering another year of security updates, pushing the Windows 11 upgrade deadline back to Oct. 12, 2027.

Microsoft officially ended support for the older OS last year but allowed users to join the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in order to maintain protection against viruses and hackers. ESU coverage was supposed to expire on Oct. 13, 2026, but the company is allowing enrolled Windows 10 users to receive monthly patches for another year—and it's not too late to sign up if you haven't already.

If you're already in Microsoft's ESU program, your coverage will automatically continue through Oct. 12, 2027 without any additional action on your part. If you haven't, though, you can enroll in ESU at any time until the program ends next year. To be eligible, your device must be running Windows 10 version 22H2 Home, Professional, Pro Education, or Workstations editions and have the latest Windows update installed. You must also be signed into a Microsoft account with administrator status.

Windows users were originally able to purchase ESU coverage for $30, and Microsoft later added the option to either redeem 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points or opt into Windows Backup to get protection for free. To check your coverage or sign up, go to Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update and look for an ESU enrollment link (visible if your device is eligible). Follow the prompts to sign into your Microsoft account and choose your enrollment option. If you've already purchased an ESU license, you can apply it to up to 10 devices running Windows 10 as long as they are linked to your Microsoft account.

The ESU program does not include any new features or non-security updates, but if you want to stay on Windows 10, it's highly recommended that you enroll in the program. Microsoft has started pushing hundreds of critical security fixes each month—a handful of which have been actively exploited zero-days—so you should ensure your device stays protected for as long as possible.

title: Five Hacks Every Garmin Fenix 9 Pro User Should Know
description: Garmin's most advanced adventure watch can get even better.
fullText:
Garmin’s new Fenix 9 Pro is a damn good watch. Mapping is fast and clear, the titanium case feels durable yet lightweight, and the built-in flashlight is a must-have—although this all comes at a steep price of $1,099.99. Whether you were first in line to order this latest Fenix, or you’re still considering if it’s right for you, here are five tips to get even more out of one of the best adventure watches money can buy.

The Fenix 9 Pro is Garmin’s most advanced mapping watch yet, so it’s fitting that there’s a lot of ground to cover here. One of my favorite small-but-mighty upgrades has been to add my route map as a dedicated data screen, and then overlay live stats, such as pace, heart rate, and distance, along the top. The payoff is that you can see where you are on the route and how hard you're working in one glance, with no flipping between screens mid-climb or mid-intersection.

First, make sure you have your map as its own dedicated data screen.

Press the START/STOP button (top right) from the watch face and select your preferred GPS activity (e.g., Run or Trail Run).

Scroll down and select Activity Settings.

Scroll all the way down and select Add New.

Next, here’s how to overlay your live stats.

While still in the Data Screens menu, scroll to your newly added Map screen and select it (press START/STOP).

Select Layout to change how many data fields overlay on the map. Scroll or use the UP and DOWN buttons to cycle through options (typically allowing one to two data fields overlaid at the top or bottom).

Click on a specific flashing field, browse through the data categories (e.g., Pace, Heart Rate Fields, or Distance), and assign your desired metric to that slot.

While messing around with maps, here are few more tricks worth mentioning:

Use "Record Only" mode as a breadcrumb trail. On an unfamiliar route, the watch quietly lays down your path without following a preloaded course. If you get turned around, you can use that trail to retrace your steps back to the start.

Try a round-trip course. Tell the watch how far you want to go, and it generates a loop that starts and ends where you are. It's ideal for traveling, or for days when you want a run or ride without planning anything.

Turn on tilted perspective maps. The 3D-style view makes terrain easier to read at a glance and pans more smoothly while you navigate trails.

For the best GPS accuracy, choose the multi-band, all-systems GPS mode in your activity settings. Then stand still for a few seconds outdoors and let the watch lock onto satellites before you hit start. Keep the sync and software updates current, too, since fresh satellite data speeds up locking. The tradeoff is battery life, so save the most accurate mode for races, technical terrain, and city canyons where signals bounce.

If you hike, add Climb Pro to a data screen. When you're following a course, it shows the climbs coming up, including how much ascent is left and the grade. You can add it in the activity's data screen settings. Knowing a steep pitch is 400 feet away is a big help when you're deciding how to pace yourself.

Go to Menu > Watch Settings > System > Shortcuts and assign quick actions, such as saving your current location or launching the stopwatch, to button combinations like hold Start + Up.

It's always worth messing around with the defaults. For instance, I love running in the rain, so I assigned "Hold Start + Up" to Touch Screen Toggle, which lets me lock the screen quickly in inclement weather. Another favorite is having the Down button toggle Do Not Disturb. The default route means holding the LIGHT button to open the Controls Menu and then selecting the Do Not Disturb icon, which is a few too many steps when I'm in a "do not disturb" mood.

If you're a regular interval trainer, I recommend assigning your lap button to also trigger auto-pause. It sounds small, but it's a nice way to cut fumbling when you'd otherwise have to manually stop and restart the clock between laps.

When in doubt, remember you can access the full watch manual easily: Just open Garmin Connect, tap your watch icon at the top right, and select Help to search specific features on the fly.

Your Fenix 9 can show you a huge amount of information, but sometimes less really is more. Mid-interval, pushing at an intense pace, your brain does not have the bandwidth to process eight fields of numbers. Pace, heart rate, and cadence is plenty for most workouts. Everything else, like elevation, calories, and lap count, can live on a secondary screen you glance at during recovery jogs rather than hard efforts.

You can customize in the Garmin Connect app or directly on the watch:

Press START/STOP and select the activity profile you want to edit.

Press and hold UP (or swipe) to open Activity Settings.

Choose the screen you want to edit.

Select Layout to pick the number of fields, anywhere from 1 to 8.

Select Data Fields to change what displays in each box.

When you're stripping down your data screens, consider updating your training settings so suggested workouts use heart rate zones instead of pace. As a long distance runner, I know that pace targets fall apart on hills, in heat, or on tired legs. Heart rate, meanwhile, tracks how hard your body is actually working.

Start by using the instructions above to strip your data screens to focus on heart rate metrics. Then you can take it a step further by broadcasting your heart rate.

You can customize the activity settings to broadcast your heart rate data automatically when you begin an activity. You can also do it manually:

Hold down the middle-left button and select Watch Settings.

Select Health & Wellness > Wrist Heart Rate > Broadcast Heart Rate.

Press the upper-right START button.

Open the pairing menu on the receiving device (like a bike computer or treadmill) and connect to your watch.

When you turn on the broadcast heart rate shortcut for gym sessions, compatible stair-steppers, rowers, and indoor bikes can read your pulse directly off your wrist—no chest strap required.

If you own a Fenix, I'd wager you're a multi-sport athlete. Instead of constantly editing your primary Run or Strength profile, duplicate it in Garmin Connect and build specialized versions, such as "Track Run" and "Easy Trail Run." Each can have its own data layout and alert settings, so switching workouts means picking a profile instead of rebuilding screens on the fly.

I'll also assume that you're the outdoorsy type, so here are two must-know features:

Green night-vision flashlight. The built-in LED flashlight lets you cycle past white and red to a green mode, which helps preserve your night vision.

Water eject. After a swim or a downpour, hold the upper-left button (or whichever button you've assigned to open your Controls menu), scroll to Water Ejection, and select it. The watch plays a series of tones to push water out of the speaker. Wipe it dry afterward. If you don't see the option, add it to your controls in the watch settings. The feature also runs automatically after you save or discard a swimming or water-related activity, and you can start a fake swim workout to trigger it.

title: 10 Hacks Every Proton VPN User Should Know
description: These are the best Proton VPN hacks for keeping your browsing activity private.
fullText:
A VPN—or Virtual Private Network—is a useful tool for protecting your data when browsing the internet, and Proton has one of the best VPNs on the market. Whether you're using Proton VPN to maintain your privacy or access geo-restricted content, these are the tricks you need to know.

Split tunneling allows you to route some of your internet traffic through the VPN while excluding other low-risk connections. The trade-off is a little less privacy for better speeds. With the Proton VPN app, split tunneling operates at the device level, so you can choose to include or exclude apps and IP addresses from the VPN tunnel. For example, you could opt for Exclude mode to exempt a specific browser that you use for online gaming, which would preserve speeds and protect all other traffic from your device. Or you could go with Include mode and add a browser you use only for sensitive connections, such as banking, and leave all other connections out of the tunnel.

Proton VPN has a browser extension for Chrome and Firefox, and all you need to use it is a free Proton account. Unlike the VPN app, which applies to all traffic on your device, the extension only protects traffic inside your browser. If you enable split tunneling in your browser, the VPN protects all websites by default except domains (and subdomains) you specifically add for exclusion. Alternatively, you can select Include mode, which will use the VPN on those websites only. This domain-level option means that you can reserve the VPN for sensitive sites and leave others out when you don't want any added latency.

Proton allows you to set up and save connection profiles with settings you use often so you don't have to manually select your location, protocol, and customized settings each time you want to use the VPN for a specific purpose (such as accessing restricted streaming content). Once you have a profile in place, you can simply go to the Profiles tab and select the one you want to use to connect. Recently used profiles will appear under Recents on the Home tab.

Another potential use for VPN profiles: getting around geo-targeted fare hikes on flights and hotels. Travel can be priced differently depending on where the purchase originates (and in what currency), so you may be able to get a cheaper ticket or stay by routing your traffic through the destination country (to book in the local currency), the airline's home base, or a lower-GDP region. Incognito mode itself doesn't hide your IP address, but it does make it more likely that you'll see current baseline rates.

If you have printers, speakers, media servers, or drives on your home network, you can enable LAN (local area network) connections so these devices aren't routed through the VPN tunnel and can talk directly to one another while keeping the rest of your traffic secure. This feature is available to paid subscribers, and you can toggle it on or off via Settings > Connection (specifics vary by app).

Proton uses a handful of well-regarded protocols that govern how the secure VPN tunnel is created, including OpenVPN and the faster (and open-source) WireGuard protocol. Proton also has its own custom protocol known as Stealth, designed to disguise your VPN connection by making it look like standard HTTPS web traffic. This can allow you to use a VPN even when VPN connections are blocked, such as by corporate firewalls and in countries with restrictive governments that attempt to censor internet access. You can select which protocol Proton uses in your Settings.

If you aren't sure which protocol to choose, let Proton's Smart Protocol do it for you. This setting automatically switches between protocols, so if one is blocked or dropped, it will move to another to keep your connection secure. This means you don't necessarily have to know or remember which protocol is best for any given situation, as Proton uses the fastest and most stable connection first. Note that Smart Protocol is on by default, but if you have changed your settings—such as to Stealth—and find that your connection drops when you switch networks, going back to Smart can eliminate this issue.

The kill switch is an important VPN feature that can prevent your data from being exposed if your connection drops. Proton has a standard kill switch, which triggers if your VPN connection drops by accident and blocks all internet traffic until the connection is reestablished. Users on Windows, the Linux GUI app, and iOS and iPadOS can enable an advanced kill switch, which prevents any and all traffic unless you are connected to Proton VPN. A kill switch can be especially useful on public wifi that may be targeted by hackers. The process to turn on the kill switch and adjust its settings varies across platforms and typically cannot be combined with split tunneling.

Proton has a built-in ad-blocker called NetShield, which can be used to block ads, trackers, malware, and, for Windows users, adult content. When enabled, Proton's dedicated DNS server checks domains you visit against known offenders and prevents them from loading. On most platforms, NetShield is set to protect against all of the data listed by default, but blocking ads and trackers can occasionally break websites or certain features you need when browsing. You can opt to block malware only, which will prevent your browser from loading resources from domains known to host malware and spyware. Note that NetShield is available only to paid subscribers. You can find ad block settings on the Home screen or under the NetShield tab.

Proton VPN has an anti-censorship feature known as alternative routing, which detects when a government, ISP, or network administrator has blocked Proton services and attempts to send traffic through another path. This runs in the background and kicks in only if Proton is being restricted. The trade-off here is that traffic is rerouted through third-party infrastructure, which may belong to AWS, Cloudflare, and/or Google. Proton notes that your actual data isn't exposed, but your IP address may be visible. If you prefer to keep this private, you can opt out of alternative routing in your app settings.

If you're using Proton VPN on mobile, you can set up shortcuts to turn your connection on or off based on certain triggers, such as joining a specific network or with a single tap. On iOS, combining Shortcuts with certain actions—like leaving or arriving home—can trigger a VPN connection or enable a specific VPN profile. You can also add Shortcuts to your Home screen or ask Siri to launch an action for you. Proton has a guide to possible iOS Shortcuts. There's no perfect native analogue on Android, but you can use a third-party app like Tasker or add an Android widget to your Home screen for one-tap access to Proton.

title: Irish sportspeople urge Republic of Ireland to boycott Israel game
description: More than 160 Irish sportspeople sign an open letter to urge the Republic of Ireland senior men's team to refuse to participate in their upcoming Nations League games against Israel.
fullText:
More than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group to urge the Republic of Ireland senior men's team to boycott their upcoming Nations League games against Israel.

The Republic of Ireland are due to play Israel on 27 September in Hungary before the reverse fixture in Serbia on 4 October.

The letter states that the Football Association of Ireland [FAI], Uefa and the Irish government should have intervened before this stage, but there is still time to "show the power of sport to unite".

Sportspeople such as Olympian Ciara Mageean, former Republic of Ireland footballer Louise Quinn, ex-Ireland rugby fly-half Tony Ward - who boycotted an Irish rugby tour of South Africa - and boxers Tyrone McKenna and Eric Donovan have signed the letter.

Also included in the 160 plus names are GAA's Padraig O'Hora, Joe Brolly, Colm O'Rourke, Michael Darragh Macauley, Philly McMahon, Valerie Mulcahy and Rena Buckley, as well as para-athlete Alan Dineen and ultimate frisbee's Stephen Jones, who both boycotted fixtures against Israel earlier this year.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter states.

"Putting on the Irish jersey and representing your country means something. But the Ireland we want represented is the one that remembers its roots in anti-colonial and anti-imperial resistance, which Irish sport played a large part of.

"This moment symbolises something deeper, it is bigger than sport. But in a way this IS sport.

"Not playing the game would be the most sporting thing you could do. Through your leadership and courage, it would show the power of sport to unite, remind us of the shared values that connect us all, and have an impact far beyond the game."

Uefa rejected request to keep Republic of Ireland and Israel separate - FAI

Republic of Ireland braced for testing Nations League

Hallgrimsson spoke to players individually about Israel games

In July, the FAI's General Assembly endorsed a motion for the Republic of Ireland to go ahead with their upcoming Nations League fixtures against Israel with 75 votes to 32 against and three abstentions from the 114 delegates.

The FAI had previously said boycotting the games would cause "significant and lasting harm" to Irish football as well as leading to a potential loss of 10.3m euros (£9m).

The fixture has caused much controversy with Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson adding that he spoke to players in his squad individually about the prospect of facing Israel, and "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games".

The Nations League games mark the Republic of Ireland's first competitive action since their World Cup play-off semi-final heartbreak against the Czech Republic in March.

Since the penalty shootout loss in Prague, they have played four friendlies, beating Grenada and Qatar and drawing with North Macedonia and Canada.

title: Scotland call for Montgomery as Tierney & McLean drop out
description: Blackburn Rovers midfielder Kristi Montgomery gets a first call-up for Scotland as Kieran Tierney and Kenny McLean drop out of the Nations League squad.
fullText:
Kristi Montgomery has been given a first call-up for Scotland after Kieran Tierney and Kenny McLean dropped out of the Nations League squad.

The Blackburn Rovers midfielder has been promoted from the Under-21s by new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli for the games against Slovenia (twice), Switzerland and North Macedonia.

The 22-year-old has started all eight Championship matches for Tony Mowbray's side this season.

Celtic defender Tierney and Norwich midfielder McLean have 119 international caps between them, while experienced trio Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland were unavailable before Pocognoli made his picks.

Montgomery is the eighth uncapped player in the 27-strong group, joining Luke Graham, Robbie Ure, Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh.

Oli McBurnie, Scott Bain, Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and James Wilson were recalled and Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour returns after missing the World Cup through injury.

Dominic Hyam, Lyndon Dykes, George Hirst, Grant Hanley, Anthony Ralston and Ross Stewart are among those overlooked by Pocognoli, with Manchester United teenager Tyler Fletcher in the Under-21s after taking Gilmour's place in the USA.

Tom English, BBC Scotland senior sports writer

Montgomery has been on the books at Blackburn Rovers since the age of nine, qualifying to play for Scotland through his mother. He's represented his country at Under-18s, Under-20s and Under-21s and has started the season particularly well at an albeit struggling Blackburn.

They're 16th in the Championship having diced with relegation last season, eventually finishing 20th in what was Montgomery's breakthrough season.

Club manager Mowbray has been singing his praises, saying: "He's an amazing young footballer who is playing in the battleground of the match in the middle of the pitch and is generally coming out with the ball after winning every duel he goes into."

Montgomery has played in all 10 of Blackburn's games this season and his promotion on the back of the unfortunate losses of veterans McLean and Tierney gives an already fresh-looking Scotland squad another level of interest.

Forwards: Kieron Bowie (Sassuolo), Findlay Curtis (Rangers), Ben Gannon-Doak (Bournemouth), Oli McBurnie (Hull City), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), James Wilson (Hearts)

title: Atletico hit back at Mourinho over referee complaints
description: Atletico Madrid hit back at Jose Mourinho after he complained about the refereeing in the Madrid derby.
fullText:
Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho after the Real Madrid boss arrived at his post-derby news conference on Sunday carrying printouts of screenshots displaying two incidents he believed should have resulted in red cards for Atletico.

Mourinho accused the officials of making key errors after Real were beaten 2-1 by Atletico, claiming the hosts should have been handed two red cards in the first half.

On Monday, Atletico posted twice on their X account, the first being a video showing a sheet of paper coming out of a printer with the words #StopAcosoArbitralYA, meaning "stop referee harassment now".

A second post showed a picture of Mourinho at the news conference with the same message.

The response from Atletico, whose team are coached by Diego Simeone, received two million views on X within two hours of it being posted.

Atletico often use their social media accounts to respond to rivals, repeatedly posting on X this summer to ridicule Barcelona over their pursuit of Atletico's talisman Julian Alvarez.

Alongside Mourinho's post‑match claims, the match report published on Real's website said that the derby loss was decided because of "dreadful refereeing", external by Ortiz Arias.

Mourinho's side had defender Dean Huijsen sent off early in the second half, when the game was goalless, for pulling down Atletico's Giuliano Simeone just inside the penalty area.

The match outcome was Real's second defeat of the season, having lost 1-0 to Real Betis earlier in September.

"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," Mourinho said as he showed media the printed images on sheets of A4 paper on Sunday.

"Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like.

"So I'll just have to limit myself to hugging my players, who gave it their all and played a first half, showed great class and character, setting us up perfectly to win the second half."

Simeone, when asked to respond to Mourinho's refereeing rant, said he was always respectful of everyone else's opinions.

"I understand that we're in a privileged position with a lot of public scrutiny, as coaches, and whether it's Mourinho, [Barcelona manager Hansi] Flick, [Real Betis boss Manuel] Pellegrini, me, or anyone else, we need to be careful about what we say," he said.

"We have to know how to respect others, the referees, our colleagues. And when someone crosses that line of respect, it's not right - you can't cross that line."

title: 'Real fear Littler could walk away' - darts would be loser in booing row
description: Could Luke Littler walk away from darts completely if the booing he has suffered at European tournaments continues?
fullText:
At just 19, Luke Littler has won almost every major trophy in darts.

He is a multi-millionaire with lucrative sponsorship deals and his own TV show.

But has his rapid rise turned some against him?

This past weekend the teenager was once again subjected to boos and whistles from sections of the crowd as he took to the stage at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam.

What is surprising though is that it came as 'The Nuke' was on a quest to complete a darts clean sweep by becoming the first player to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year.

Littler suggested afterwards that, if the booing continues, he will not attend events held in the Netherlands.

But Samuel Gill, editor of Dartnews.com, suggests Littler's future in the sport could be at stake.

"There's a real fear that within a few years he'll just turn around and walk away from the sport," Gill told BBC Sport.

"So, I think for fans, 'Don't bite the hand that feeds you'. If people keep taunting him and don't want him to win, he might end up just walking away and not bothering anymore."

Amsterdam was the latest tournament where Littler has faced what some might describe as an overly hostile reaction from fans.

A vibrant pantomime-style atmosphere is part and parcel of the darts experience and Dutch and German crowds are amongs the most raucous - but it is clear Littler believes he has been unfairly targeted.

The referee stopped the match during his narrow win against Nathan Aspinall in the last-16 on Saturday to warn the hostile crowd about its behaviour, before play resumed.

It followed Littler also being booed during his win against home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday.

The teenager's quarter-final defeat to Jonny Clayton ended Littler's quest for the clean sweep, but the Warrington native clearly felt fans had been unduly harsh towards him.

Littler has now withdrawn from a series of upcoming events.

"Just no point in me travelling, wasting my time while I'm getting booed," said Littler.

Littler has also been jeered at numerous events in the UK.

His phenomenal rise saw him reach the PDC World Darts Championship aged just 16 in his debut year as a professional.

He captured the title the following year and the trophies, sponsorship deals and six-figure winners' cheques have continued to flow.

But increasingly so have whistles and boos during his performances.

"I don't think people expected him to reach the heights that he has so quickly," Gill said.

The darts journalist - who became aware of Littler when the sport star was 14 - says this level of attention is not just unique to the British player.

"Michael van Gerwen was the same for a long time when he dominated the sport. He barely lost a game in about five years, and he was hoovering up titles for fun and it was similar," said Gill.

"Everyone wanted to boo him and even me as a viewer before I got into this role, growing up watching Van Gerwen, I wanted him to lose because it's something different for the sport every single week."

Currently ranked number one in the world, Littler is so far ahead of his closest rivals that he already has the advantage of only having to play in selective tournaments.

His boycott threat could end up being a blow to tournament organisers.

"They don't like him because he's that good. And he's got a bit of swagger to him," said Karl Holden secretary of St Helen's Darts Academy - where Littler honed his skills from the age of nine.

"Luke's got a bit of a character to him. For me, he's the ultimate professional. He might give a little bit of the large sometimes, but you need that, otherwise darts would be totally boring."

It seems remarkable that the future of Littler's career in the sport is even being debated.

More so when you consider his age and the fact he only turned professional two years ago.

However, Gill believes that Littler's rapid haul of trophies, coupled with the huge amounts of money now in the sport, could result in the teenager leaving in the next "four to five years" should the boos and whistles continue.

Gill believes Littler's impact on the darting world is immeasurable.

Tickets to events featuring him are often sold out, applications to darting academies are reported to be at an all-time high and the Briton has transcended the sport.

Gill therefore feels that, if Littler was to walk away, the sport would be the real loser.

"He's the one who is bringing this sport to a completely different level. Nowadays, he is back-page news wherever you go," Gill said.

"He might just decide 'I just want a quiet life now and just live off his money'."

Littler has barely known anything other than winning. His challenged now is maintaining that victorious streak while keeping fans - whose interest helps fund his prize money - happy.

Tricky when some are paying with the hope of seeing him lose.

"If he was on that stage, everybody liked him and he just threw darts, I think I'd get bored of watching him," Holden said.

title: Infantino says Fifa can change as he proposes external review
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of the governance of world football's governing body.
fullText:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates, and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino said the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

Before a meeting of the Council next month, Infantino says he is also suggesting a consultation on "how Fifa's decision-making can be further strengthened".

This would include proposals on the role of the president, as well as "practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

In what appears to be a conciliatory gesture, Infantino writes: "Over recent weeks, I have taken time to listen before writing to you", and says the consultation will be with confederations, member associations and "relevant stakeholders".

He insists that the FFE plan "did not involve relinquishing Fifa's control or authority over sporting decisions. Obviously!"

His letter adds: "The proposal entered the public domain before Fifa's planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the member associations. I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not."

Infantino also claims that "democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale. They are not for sale and never will be".

He states he remains "fully committed to leading Fifa and confident in what we can achieve together".

Infantino's letter comes after Uefa and Concacaf - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members from its cash reserves.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Infantino claims that the collapse of FFE "does not diminish our ambition or our responsibility to invest more of Fifa's success back into football.

"We will continue to explore sustainable ways to grow Fifa's resources and expand development and solidarity support for every member association. What changes is not the ambition, but the strength of the process through which major ideas are developed, tested and decided.

"The progress we have made over the past decade gives us a strong foundation for the future. It also gives us the confidence to examine whether our governance remains suited to the scale and complexity of the decisions ahead."

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss-Italian Fifa leader will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Last month, European football's governing body Uefa began preparing criminal legal proceedings against Infantino at courts in the US over the FFE plan, demanding the release of all documents.

Fifa hit back and accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to the litigation.

Having defiantly clung to power for weeks amid an unprecedented rebellion over his presidency, this is a significant change in tone from Infantino - and the first sign that he may feel he has no choice but to compromise if he is to win another re-election in March.

On October 15th, Fifa's Council will meet for the first time since this crisis began, and Infantino will no doubt hope that this relieves some of the pressure he is under.

But even if he is prepared to accept some changes to the way Fifa is run, will that be enough to win over some of those that have turned against him?

As well as wanting him to step down, many of Infantino's critics want an overhaul of Fifa's governance, with curbs on the president's power (such as a maximum of a single term in office), more separation between the president and the Fifa administration, greater emphasis on human rights and sustainability, and the redistribution of Fifa's cash reserves.

It will be fascinating to see if Infantino is prepared to accept such changes if it means staying in power.

Unrivaled women's basketball tour to play in Houston in February
description: The 3-on-3 league, which features many of women's basketball 's top players, will make a Houston a stop on its nationwide tour.
fullText:
Unrivaled, the 3-on-3 women's basketball league featuring many of the sport's best players, is coming to Houston.

The league announced Monday that it will play a doubleheader at Toyota Center on Feb. 12 as part of its nationwide tour.

Unrivaled's Chief Growth Officer Chloe Pavlech told the Chronicle that the decision to come to Houston was a no-brainer due to the city's history of women's basketball and the excitement of people in the local community.

The doubleheader will also be a harbinger for fans looking forward to welcoming the Houston Comets back to the WNBA later in 2027.

"We already know the city is super excited to bring women's basketball back to Houston," Pavlech said. "To be able to piggyback off of that announcement, and then with Houston locals and people coming in from surrounding cities to be able to just experience it, it's just going to be one of the peaks and the heights of women's basketball."

Unrivaled, which runs during the WNBA offseason, debuted in 2025, playing all of its games in Miami. South Florida remains the hub for most of its games but the league now also goes on a tour to bring the league to other cities during the season. The first tour last year took games on the road to Philadelphia and New York City.

The 2027 season's tour will have eight stops across the country. New York City, Boston, Philadelphia, Detroit and Minneapolis will also host tour stops with two more locations scheduled to be announced.

"I know our players are super excited to come to Houston," Pavlech said.

Among the players signed to play in the league this year include league co-founders Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, Dallas Wings star Paige Bueckers, rookie phenom Olivia Miles and four-time WNBA champion Chelsea Gray.

Aaliyah Edwards is also currently scheduled to play in 2027, per the league website. Edwards plays for the Connecticut Sun in the WNBA, who are moving to Houston at the conclusion of the year.

The 2026 season lasted from January to March with eight total teams.

Tickets for the tour stop go on sale Monday at noon. Unrivaled will also host an event Monday starting at 7 p.m. at Side Peace as part of its announcement of the tour stop as well as kicking off a partnership for local watch parties that will continue during the season.

"We want to be able to keep showing up," Pavelch said. "We want to be able to keep the community energized."

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle. 

This article originally published at Unrivaled women's basketball tour to play in Houston in February.

title: Lisandro Martinez: Man United star sets unwanted club record in Fulham draw
description: 1Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez equalled an unwanted record after scoring an own goal against Fulham on Sunday, 20 September. The Cottagers looked set to pick up their first Premier Leag...
fullText:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez equalled an unwanted record after scoring an own goal against Fulham on Sunday, 20 September. The Cottagers looked set to pick up their first Premier League win of the season before Matheus Cunha scored an 89th-minute equaliser and helped secure a point for the Red Devils.

While United narrowly escaped registering a third defeat in as many games, it would have done little to ease the frustrations of their supporters. The English giants have failed to take the step forward after finishing third in the league last season.

United have registered just one win in five games in the Premier League so far, losing two games, and sit 12th in the table. They were knocked out of the EFL Cup by Brighton & Hove Albion last week in the third round.

While the Red Devils have failed to impress in the final third, their defending has hardly been convincing either. Martinez, who reached the 2026 FIFA World Cup final over the summer, has endured a mixed start to the new campaign.

Martinez was a first-team regular for United in the second half of last season, playing a major role in the club's rise under Michael Carrick. Over the summer, the Argentine defender displayed his ball-playing capabilities at the grandest stage with his country, helping them reach the World Cup final.

Unfortunately, Martinez picked up an injury in the final against Spain, who went on to pick up a 1-0 win. The 28 year old began the new season from the bench for the opening-day defeat to Hull City, before making his first start in the 5-2 win against Ipswich Town.

The Argentine has played every minute of every Premier League game since and also started in the opening Champions League tie earlier this month against Sabah. Martinez scored his first-ever goal in the premier European club competition, while also helping United keep a clean sheet in the 4-0 win.

However, the former Ajax man had a nightmare outing against Fulham this weekend and inadvertently wrote his name into the record books.

Martinez has now scored three own goals in the Premier League since arriving at Old Trafford in the summer of 2022, the joint-most for the club since the inception of the league. This unwanted feat places him alongside former players Jonny Evans, Henning Berg, Wes Brown and John O'Shea.

The Argentine also scored an unfortunate own goal last season in the 3-2 win over Arsenal at Old Trafford, in what was Carrick's second game in charge. United, however, rallied to win the game that night, when Bryan Mbeumo, Patrick Dorgu and Cunha found the back of the net.

Meanwhile, Martinez's first own goal for United came in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur in the 2023/24 campaign.

Martinez would hate to be the first player to score four own goals for United in the Premier League era. Meanwhile, the Argentine's contract expires at the end of this season, so INEOS also have a big decision on their hands in the coming months.

title: What Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said about QB Michael Penix Jr.'s return
description: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski didn’t rule out the possibility that QB Michael Penix Jr. will return from injury on Thursday night. Here's the latest.
fullText:
ATLANTA – No news is good news?

Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski didn't rule out the possibility that quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will make his long-awaited return on Thursday night against the Green Bay Packers.

But he didn't commit to such a plan, either, during a virtual press conference early Monday afternoon.

"I will let you guys know," Stefanski said, a day after the Falcons (0-2) were blasted 34-3 by the Carolina Panthers and third-string quarterback Cooper Rush was benched for undrafted rookie Jack Strand.

"I will give you an update when I've been able to talk to the players and work through it. So, I don't have an update right this minute. But again, constant communication with Mike, with all of our guys, so we'll work through it this week."

Asked about reports that suggest Penix, recovering from knee surgery, is trending toward playing this week, Stefanski said, "I can't comment on reports. I will tell you, I want to make sure I talk to our players first."

Stefanski said players were due to report to the team's headquarters at noon on Monday for a weightlifting session. He said he could provide an update later on Monday after team meetings.

Penix was medically cleared in late August to fully participate in practices, yet having suffered three torn ACL injuries during his pro and college careers, has been cautious in declaring himself ready to play.

In the meantime, the Falcons offense has been a mess – failing to advance a single drive to the red zone in the first two games.

In addition to Penix, the status of Tua Tagovailoa – named the starter for Week 1 before suffering an oblique injury during warmups for a practice three days before the opener – is also fluid.

Of Tagovailoa, Stefanski said: "Getting better. We'll work through it."

title: Avonte Maddox out for year, as Lions seek DB ‘shake up’
description: Detroit Lions safety Avonte Maddox is out for the year, and now the team is promising shake ups in the secondary.
fullText:
Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered tough injury news on Monday, noting that veteran safety Avonte Maddox will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a foot injury on Thursday night that will require surgery.

"That hurts a little bit," Campbell said. "Maddox is a good player for us. Good solid football player, headsy. I hate that for him. But that's the hand that we're dealt, and we move forward."

Maddox was starting for the Lions at safety for the first two weeks of the season while Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch remain on the Physically Unable to Perform list. Both Joseph and Branch are eligible to return to practice this week, Campbell noted that both still need more time.

That leaves the Lions in a bit of a precarious spot at safety moving forward. Detroit has Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper capable of stepping in and starting, but the depth behind that only currently includes Christian Izien—who has been playing more nickel lately.

The Lions have reportedly been in search for some veteran safety help on the free agent market, and held a workout on Monday morning that reportedly included Jordan Fuller, Jalen Mills, and Mike Edwards, among others. Campbell noted that the search won't just be limited to available veterans, either.

"We had a workout this morning just looking for a veteran guy, and we're looking for some of these safeties that are on other teams right now that are promising young players that we could potentially poach and bring in and let them compete," Campbell said. "Right now, we've got Chuck and Izzy and Harper, but we need to bring in some fresh players and get a look at them."

Beyond just being shorthanded at safety, the Lions also clearly need to shake up their secondary after two rough defensive performances to start the season. Campbell certainly hinted that some depth chart reorganization could be on the horizon.

"We're going to do a couple of things defensively, we're going to move some guys around, we're going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and shake it up a little bit," Campbell said. "And because they've earned that. We've got some guys in here that have earned some play time that they deserve a chance to do more for us."

Campbell was asked specifically about two players who have started the season on the inactive list: defensive end Ahmed Hassanein and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw. The Lions coach didn't exactly sound eager about throwing them into the lineup, but didn't count it out either.

"Right now I'm open to everything," Campbell said. "I'm open and we're looking at everything. So, yeah, there's always a chance."

title: Saints receive multiple Madden rating updates after must-see start
description: Several New Orleans Saints players saw their Madden 27 grades improve after a must-see start to the 2026 season. But Tyler Shough isn't one of them.
fullText:
Week 1 for the New Orleans Saints was a thrilling one, as they took on the Detroit Lions on the road and lost in overtime on a failed two-point conversion attempt. However, they showed some extreme resiliency and found their stride on offense in the second half, especially Tyler Shough and Chris Olave.

This strong performance from them led to some Madden 27 ratings being updated, with five players receiving increased overall stats and one receiving a decrease. Here is the full list of players to get an update following Week 1:

WR Chris Olave - 87 overall to 88 overall (+1)

EDGE Chase Young - 81 overall to 82 overall (+1)

LT Kelvin Banks Jr. - 77 overall to 78 overall (+1)

RT Taliese Fuaga - 77 overall to 76 overall (-1)

WR Devaughn Vele - 74 overall to 75 overall (+1)

DT Vernon Broughton - 68 overall to 69 overall (+1)

There are a couple of surprises here, either in the changes or the lack thereof. Olave only receiving one additional rating point, despite catching 10 of a whopping 13 targets for 182 yards, seems a little low. Especially considering Justin Jefferson, who was already a 94, got two more points for putting up 8 receptions on 9 targets for 92 yards and 2 touchdowns.

Tyler Shough also not receiving any upgrade at all from his current 77 rating is asinine, following a performance where he had the most single-game passing yards for the Saints since Week 1 of 2018. David Edwards is also only a 79 still, which, after an outstanding 2025 campaign and Week 1, feels ridiculously low.

We will see what updates come through following their huge win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2, a team that Madden has given some lofty ratings to and believes will be one of the best in the NFL this season.
