title: Panthers produce stunning 56-point turnaround after historic embarrassment
description: Carolina allowed a franchise-record 59 points in Week 1, then delivered one of Sunday’s most dominant victories.
fullText:
Panthers produce stunning 56-point turnaround after historic embarrassment originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Seven days completely changed the conversation surrounding the Carolina Panthers. Carolina surrendered a franchise-record 59 points in its season-opening loss to the Chicago Bears. The defensive performance created immediate questions about the team's toughness, preparation and ability to compete in the NFC South.

The Panthers answered every one of them Sunday. Carolina demolished the Atlanta Falcons 34-3 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, producing a 56-point improvement in scoring margin from one week to the next.

Bryce Young threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Devin Lloyd intercepted two passes, returned one for a touchdown and helped the Panthers force five Atlanta turnovers.

The result was not merely a bounce-back victory.

Young has thrown six touchdown passes through Carolina's first two games and added another score on the ground. His three-touchdown performance against Atlanta pushed his passer rating for the season to 113.3. Young found veteran tight end Darren Waller for two touchdowns. Waller's production carried additional meaning because the game marked his first appearance in his hometown of Atlanta in six years.

Tetairoa McMillan added five receptions for 101 yards, giving Young a dynamic downfield option. Xavier Legette produced a 55-yard reception that helped Carolina establish control early.

The Panthers led 20-3 at halftime and never allowed Atlanta to threaten.

That represented a dramatic change from Week 1, when Carolina's defense appeared incapable of generating a stop.

MORE: Caleb Williams injury overshadows Bears' brutal loss to Vikings

Lloyd was involved in nearly every important defensive moment. The linebacker forced a fumble from Cooper Rush and recorded two interceptions. His second pick came on rookie Jack Strand's first NFL pass, which Lloyd returned for a touchdown.

Atlanta committed turnovers with both quarterbacks and failed to reach the red zone for the second consecutive game.

Rush completed passes for only 86 yards before being replaced. Strand's introduction produced an immediate defensive touchdown for Carolina. The Falcons fell to 0-2 and left the afternoon with major questions about their quarterback situation and offensive structure.

Carolina faced an entirely different reality.

The Panthers became only the fifth team in franchise history to score at least 30 points in a road victory. More importantly, they demonstrated that their disastrous opener did not have to define their season.

Young looked decisive. Waller looked healthy. McMillan looked capable of becoming a featured receiver. The defense played with the aggression and discipline missing against Chicago.

One dominant afternoon does not erase every concern created by allowing 59 points. It does prove the Panthers were capable of responding rather than unraveling. Carolina's scoring margin moved from minus-22 in Week 1 to plus-31 in Week 2.

A 56-point swing in seven days might be the most unexpected statistic of the NFL weekend.

title: Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase join exclusive NFL club in Bengals’ win vs. Texans
description: One of the greatest QB-WR duos in NFL history.
fullText:
Joe Burrow has started slowly in nearly every season of his career. He hasn't been prolific through two games this season, but he's been successful.

In addition, he's joined some elite company alongside his running mate, Ja'Marr Chase.

For only the second time in his career, Burrow has thrown for 200+ yards in each of his first two games of the season. Sunday in Houston, Burrow threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns on 20/31 passing with no interceptions.

Both touchdowns went to Chase, giving the duo 50 touchdown connections for their career. According to NFL researcher Arye Pulli, only four QB-WR duos in NFL history have hit that mark before reaching the age of 30, and the Burrow-Chase duo just joined the club.

Chase finished the game with seven catches for 75 yards and those two scores.

QB-WR duos in NFL history to reach 50 touchdown connections while both players were under 30:

🏈 Dan Marino — Mark Clayton
🏈 John Hadl — Lance Alworth
🏈 Daunte Culpepper — Randy Moss
🏈 Joe Burrow — Ja’Marr Chase

That’s the entire list.

Again, Burrow hasn't been prolific yet. But he's been productive and successful.

On Sunday, Burrow also showed his toughness as he dealt with back tightness during the week leading up to Sunday. Not ideal going up against the Texans' defense. But Burrow wasn't mincing words or backing down earlier this week when he said he was good to go.

On Sunday in Houston, Burrow went out and withstood five sacks, delivering a performance that helped the Bengals to a massive road win.

We've seen Burrow deliver performances like this while banged up and taking several hits in a game. Houston's defense is ferocious, and they sacked Burrow five times on Sunday. Yet Burrow extended plays, including the second touchdown to Chase and a 16-yard third-down pass to Samaje Perine.

Despite back tightness and Houston's defense, Burrow overcame it all, and the Bengals are now 2-0. Just wait till he starts posting prolific numbers.

fullText:
Ole Miss football news: Kewan Lacy's shoulder MRI reveals huge update appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Coach Pete Golding's Ole Miss football team scored perhaps the biggest win of Week 3 in college football, beating LSU 32-24 on a day when QB Trinidad Chambliss looked like a Heisman favorite. Star running back Kewan Lacy scored the first touchdown of the day for Golding's squad but left with a worrisome shoulder injury.

Lacy's injury looked bad, but there is now hope for a return based on a report from ESPN's Pete Thamel.

"Sources: Ole Miss star running back Kewan Lacy had an MRI on his shoulder today, and the injury is not expected to be long term. He's uncertain for the game at Florida on Saturday, as he'll be monitored this week to gauge his recovery."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Ole Miss has a big target on its back after ascending to the fourth spot in the latest rankings. The Rebels' rushing attack looked strong in the early going against coach Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers, but finished with just over 60 yards as Chambliss and the passing game carried the load in Lacy's absence.

Lacy's backup is JT Lindsey, who looked good in limited action vs. the Tigers with four carries for 20 yards, an average of five yards per carry. Chambliss has the ability to scramble for yardage and throw on the run, which could help keep the Gators' defense at bay in Week 4.

September 26's game at The Swamp now looks like one of the biggest on the college football calendar, a testament to the Rebels' big win, and talented team. Coach Golding knows the SEC schedule won't get any easier, and he also knows all too well about the immense talents Lacy brings to the table. Ole Miss' depth will be tested, and Lindsey could soon find himself in the spotlight as the Rebels look to win their fourth game in four tries.

title: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin offers excellent analysis of offensive struggles
description: Sunday's performance by the Steelers offense reminded of the team under Mike Tomlin and he talked about what he saw after the loss.
fullText:
Sunday's offensive performance by the Pittsburgh Steelers was forgettable to say the least. There was nothing about what the Steelers did on offense against the New England Patriots to take away as a positive. Pittsburgh failed to score a touchdown and finished with just 235 total yards of offense.

Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, who is now an analyst for NBC, was asked for his thoughts on the game and he was very honest in his evaluation, even though the game reminded us a great deal of the offense from many games in the Tomlin era.

"From my perspective, they don't have a place to hang their hat," Tomlin said. "They haven't established the run. They're not performing well enough on third-down or possession-down circumstances. And to make matters worse, they're not getting yards in chunks. They can't solve all their problems, but they better solve at least one of these problems, and really soon."

All of the problems with the Steelers center on two factors. One, they have invested heavily in the offensive line and it hasn't paid off and two, the skill position players on the team lack any level of explosion, which just congests the offense at the line of scrimmage or in coverage. These aren't coaching fixes; they are roster fixes, and right now there aren't any players available short of pulling off some big trades to correct these problems during the season.

This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin offers excellent analysis of offensive struggles

title: Former Falcons QB tied for most TD passes in NFL after Week 2
description: Former Falcons QB Kirk Cousins has NFL-high six TD passes for 2-0 Raiders
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons dropped to 0-2 after Sunday's embarrassing 34-3 blowout against the Carolina Panthers. Things got so bad that the Falcons turned to fourth-string quarterback Jack Strand in the third quarter of their Week 2 loss.

As if Sunday's game wasn't bad enough, former Falcons quarterback Kirk Cousins added insult to injury with his latest performance. Cousins passed for three touchdowns and an interception in the Raiders' 26-14 upset over the Los Angeles Chargers.

The 38-year-old is tied for the league lead with six touchdowns passes and has the Raiders sitting at 2-0 after Week 2. The Falcons released Cousins in March, ending his frustrating two-year run in Atlanta.

Las Vegas signed the veteran QB to help mentor No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but they didn't make the mistake of giving Cousins $100 million in guaranteed money. Some thought the Falcons might bring back Cousins to reunite with Kevin Stefanski, but both sides needed a fresh start.

The Falcons have struggled to navigate their quarterback injuries thus far, and Cooper Rush hasn't gotten the job done. Rush was benched in the third quarter for Strand on Sunday, but the rookie didn't fare much better. Atlanta's quarterbacks combined to go 18/32 for 129 yards and three interceptions.

On the bright side, Michael Penix Jr. is expected to return next week. However, we will have to wait and see what Kevin Stefanski says on Monday morning.

This article originally appeared on Falcons Wire: Former Falcons QB tied for most TD passes in NFL after Week 2

title: Iga Swiatek’s former coach knows exactly why she lost in the fourth round of the US Open
description: Iga Swiatek came into the US Open with newfound confidence, but that didn’t translate to results. The Pole had ended her title drought at the...
fullText:
Iga Swiatek came into the US Open with newfound confidence, but that didn't translate to results.

The Pole had ended her title drought at the Canadian Open with a resurgent run before reaching the semifinals of the Cincinnati Open.

Swiatek then started well in New York, winning her first three matches without dropping a set.

But she ended up losing to Qinwen Zheng in the fourth round, falling 7-5, 6-3 to the Chinese player.

Two weeks after her exit, Swiatek's old coach, Katerina Urbanova, provided an explanation for the defeat.

As per sport.pl, Urbanova was asked if she saw the loss to Zheng coming.

She replied: "I had noticed it before. It was different in the third-round US Open match against Marie Bouzková.

"The Czech player played well. Poles thought that she played at a very high level, though in my opinion, it was just her normal.

"However, the situation favoured Iga in that match because Bouzkov hits shorter balls, so Iga could capitalise on those with the power of her own shots.

"If we go back to the match with Zheng, you could see that the Chinese player began hitting high balls that landed deep near the baseline, whereas she had previously played shorter balls and mixed up her style.

"This variation threw Iga off. At the same time, while she had been returning very well leading up to the match against Zheng, that return game was missing in this last match."

"She has reverted to the issues she's been dealing with all season. She did have a better run in recent weeks, winning the tournament in Toronto and reaching the semifinals in Cincinnati.

"However, she still lacks self-confidence. We also have to remember that her rivals now know how to play against her. It only takes a few slower balls to make Iga start committing errors. She struggles most with so-called "dead balls"- shots where she has to generate her own pace.

"That's when she starts missing often. Her opponents know this and force her into committing errors, particularly on the forehand side."

Asked how Swiatek can deal with her ongoing issues, Urbanova responded: "The problem is that tennis is constantly evolving, and her power no longer makes quite the same impression. An important technical challenge is still her forehand grip; it is unconventional and requires work.

"Perhaps her Spanish coach can manage to make changes? I see him trying to get Iga to stay lower on her legs.

"She has stopped jumping into her shots and is now more grounded; this will allow for greater stability over time. Iga is having a really poor season, but things have started moving in the right direction since Wimbledon.

"Even before the US Open, her serving has improved and she was returning well. However, when those elements falter, she reverts to old habits, playing too cautiously.

"She is afraid to pull the trigger at certain moments and slows down her swing. What worries me – as a coach who has known her since childhood – is that Iga sometimes lacks courage on the court; she retreats during rallies or at specific stages of a match."

Swiatek's results this year have seen her fall to ninth in the WTA rankings.

title: Cubs’ Alex Bregman shares selfie showing damage from foul ball to face
description: A foul ball left Alex Bregman with significant facial injuries.
fullText:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman shared a graphic selfie Sunday after suffering a frightening facial injury from a foul ball during an MLB game.

Bregman was struck during the fourth inning of Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Teammate Michael Busch fouled a pitch from Luis Mey, and the ball bounced into Bregman while he stood near the on-deck circle.

Bregman immediately left the game with blood visible on his face. He later underwent hospital testing after the ball struck him near his cheekbone.

MORE: Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants

The selfie, which he shared on his Instagram, showed significant swelling around Bregman's eye, along with facial cuts and a nosebleed. Especially the area below his eye had turned slightly black. He also included a message for supporters: "Thanks for all the messages, y'all. I'll be back 🙏."

Cubs manager Craig Counsell described the incident as a "terrible, terrible accident." He said the team's priority was getting positive medical results after Bregman was taken to the hospital.

The injury came during an important stretch for Chicago. The Cubs entered Sunday chasing a postseason berth and remained positioned for a National League wild-card spot.

Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman (3) walks off the field after getting hit by a foul ball in the fourth inning in the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Bregman had already contributed during Sunday's game before leaving. He delivered an RBI single in the first inning, helping Chicago build an early lead.

After Bregman exited, Matt Shaw replaced him as a pinch-hitter. Pedro Ramirez shifted to third base while Shaw moved to second.

The Cubs continued producing offensively without their veteran third baseman. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run, while Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered.

MORE: Yankees make sudden change to lineup, remove breakout star

Chicago now faces a balance between its postseason push and Bregman's recovery. His defensive stability and veteran experience remain valuable during the final week.

Counsell said Bregman's general well-being came before baseball considerations. "I want to get a good report first," the manager said.

Bregman's message offered some optimism, but his return timeline remains unclear. The Cubs will need to await further medical updates before determining his availability.

title: Croatia Forward Boris Tisma No Longer Part of Washington Basketball
description: One of the Washington Huskies' incoming international signings is no longer set to play for Danny Sprinkle.
fullText:
Despite appearing in practice footage over the past couple of months, incoming Croatian forward Boris Tisma is no longer set to play for the Washington Huskies in the 2026-27 season.

Tisma, one of several reported international signings for UW coach Danny Sprinkle this offseason, has now signed a two-year contract with Movistar Estudiantes, a professional team based in Madrid, Spain. He previously played for Real Madrid in 2020-21 and was then loaned out to another Liga ACB team in 2021.

Prior to the 6-foot-9 power forward's move to America, he played for two teams in Croatia—Split (2022-25) and Zadar (2025-26)—and one SC Derby in Montenegro, proving to be a rising international prospect that attracted the attention of several schools, including UW.

📝 OFICIAL 

Boris Tisma, nuevo jugador de Movistar Estudiantes.

El ala-pívot croata (2,04 m, 2002) se incorpora al equipo para las dos próximas temporadas. 🇭🇷

¡Bienvenido, Boris! 💙

👇https://t.co/pTOdmOqkig pic.twitter.com/KS3dzh0ECT

The departure of Tisma isn't surprising in the wake of the NCAA changing eligibility requirements for international players coming to the United States back in May. Any player who has signed a professional contract prior to coming to the States now loses their eligibility, though it's unclear if that's the specific reason why UW and Tisma parted.

In the past two months, the Huskies have added a pair of transfers, former Rutgers guard Harun Zrno and ex-Nevada guard Tayshawn Comer, but still have a void to fill in the post with the loss of Tisma. UW has not released its 2026-27 roster on the school's website with less than one month until Sprinkle's team hits the road to face Boise State in a preseason exhibition on October 17 at Idaho Central Arena.

As of now, UW has five bigs going into year three under Sprinkle: second-year forwards Jasir Rencher and Nikola Dzepina, third-year center Lathan Somerville, fourth-year forward Mady Traore, and incoming fourth-year transfer LeJuan Watts.

title: Zach Johnson wins at Pebble Beach for 2nd straight Champions victory and 6th of the season
description: Zach Johnson won the Pure Insurance Championship on Sunday at foggy Pebble Beach for his second straight PGA Tour Champions victory and the sixth in his first season on the 50-and-over circuit.
fullText:
PEBBLE BEACH, Calif. — Zach Johnson won the Pure Insurance Championship on Sunday at foggy Pebble Beach for his second straight PGA Tour Champions victory and the sixth in his first season on the 50-and-over circuit.

Johnson broke a tie with Stewart Cink for the tour victory lead, closing with a 7-under 65 for a two-stroke victory over former LIV player Henrik Stenson, Steven Alker and early starter Rory Sabbatini. Johnson, the Sanford International winner last week in South Dakota, had a 14-under 202 total.

Johnson won the six titles in only 15 starts. The Iowa native won 12 times on the PGA Tour, highlighted by major titles at the 2007 Masters and 2015 British Open.

Sabbatini shot a 63 — the best round of the week — to post at 12 under. He parred the final two holes, finishing as the other leaders were playing the first few holes on the back nine.

Johnson — who eagled the par-4 second — birdied the par-4 11th to join Sabbatini at 12 under, and took the lead with a birdie on the par-4 13th.

Johnson played an aggressive line off the tee on the par-5 18th and reached the green in two. He two-putted from 35 feet for birdie — holing a 3-footer.

Stenson closed with a 68 playing alongside Johnson.

Alker had a 67. He was coming off three straight victories, one of them on the Legends Tour in Europe.

The players were paired with juniors of The First Tee program from chapters across the country.

title: Ja’Marr Chase makes honest admission after incredible Bengals TD
description: Ja’Marr Chase explained how he made a spectacular 32-yard touchdown catch in the Cincinnati Bengals’ Week 2 win over the Houston Texans.
fullText:
Ja'Marr Chase turned uncertainty into a catch-of-the-year contender during the Cincinnati Bengals' 20-6 win over the Houston Texans.

Joe Burrow targeted Chase down the right sideline late in the second quarter. Chase briefly lost track of the football while battling All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr., but recovered in time to secure the pass and tap both feet down near the pylon for a 32-yard touchdown.

WHAT A CATCH BY JA'MARR CHASE FOR THE TD pic.twitter.com/M1vbRIiESS

The jaw-dropping play gave Cincinnati a 7-3 lead it never surrendered. In the locker room after the game, Chase admitted his adjustment came entirely on instinct

"I literally don't know what I did," Chase said in a postgame interview with CLNS reporter Mike Petraglia. "Like, I couldn't see the ball for a second, and I was just fighting, trying to get in position. But by the time I seen the ball, it was like in a light, and it came real fast, and it was just adjustment."

But by the time I seen the ball, it was like in a light, and it came real fast, and… pic.twitter.com/nxA9QTvM6J

Chase later caught an 18-yard touchdown from Burrow in the third quarter, helping the Bengals improve to 2-0 for a second consecutive season. He finished with seven receptions for 75 yards and two scores after being held to two catches for 12 yards in the opener.

Burrow completed 20 of 31 passes for 207 yards and the two touchdowns. Chase's first score accounted for Cincinnati's only points of the opening half before the Bengals pulled away following halftime.

title: Mike Tomlin responds to Todd Monken's post-game comments

fullText:
The rivalry between the Browns and Steelers is never going to be non-personal for fans or everyone involved at every level of both teams. Even when people are removed from the rivalry, the animosity remains in place.

title: Troy Melton injury update as Tigers RHP says 'twinges' chased him
description: Detroit Tigers righty Troy Melton exited Sunday in the fourth inning in Chicago, but he said he doesn't think it's a serious arm injury.
fullText:
CHICAGO – Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Troy Melton experienced forearm tightness and soreness in his throwing arm while pitching in the fourth inning against the Chicago White Sox on Sunday, Sept. 20.

He was taken out of the game and will undergo tests on Monday.

"It's just general tightness and soreness," Melton said after the Tigers lost 8-1 at Rate Field, ending any hopes of the postseason. "There are days where you get twinges like that, and it goes away. You don't think about it again. Then you do some work on it, and it's gone. It just never went away."

SUNDAY'S ACTION: Detroit Tigers playoff hopes end with soggy spanking in Chicago

Any issues with Melton's throwing arm raise instant concerns because he had issues earlier this season. Melton, 25, was diagnosed in late February with right elbow inflammation. He went on the 60-day injured list and returned to action May 24.

"It's hard without knowing exactly for sure what's going on, but I don't think they're related," Melton said. "As of what I know right now, I wouldn't say they're similar. I mean, obviously similar body part, I guess, but I don't think it's the same thing."

Melton was not sharp in this game. He threw just 47 of his 83 pitches for strikes. He said he started to feel the forearm issue while warming up before the fourth inning. "I kind of felt a little bit of tightness just in my forearm and kind of expected it to go away," he said. "It kind of just never did. It got achy and tight on me pretty quick and never got any better as the inning progressed. So just kind of stayed tight."

He tried to stretch out his arm on the mound. "Without raising super alarm flags," he said. "There was no individual pitch that set it off or anything like that."

Tigers catcher Eduardo Valencia noticed something wrong and went to the mound.

"I was good enough to go for the next hitter," Melton said. "I was just trying to get it to a place where it felt better, and just never did."

Tigers pitching coach Chris Fetter went out to the mound. As soon as Fetter heard about the arm issue, he motioned for Tigers manager A.J. Hinch and a trainer to come to the mound.

"Fett went out to just calm down the inning in the moment," Hinch said. "Then when Fett turned around, that's when I went out. So Troy just said he didn't feel great, so we're gonna get him checked out."

He will undergo tests on Monday.

"He reported some achiness and some issue with his arm, so I we're gonna get him checked out [Monday], kind of full examination," Hinch said. "As soon as he started saying he was uncomfortable, we took him out of the game. So I haven't seen him since, and we'll hope for the best tomorrow. But we'll see how the how the tests come back.

Melton was taken out with the White Sox holding a 3-0 lead. He threw 3⅔ innings, giving up four hits and four runs. He struck out four while walking three.

"I saw the non-command, but there was no issue until Fett motioned me out," Hinch said.

The game started after a 3-hour, 50-minute rain delay. With just a week left in the regular season and no shared open dates, they had to get this game in because the White Sox are fighting for the playoffs. So, they started in a rainstorm. It looked like it was raining sideways, as fans sat in the stands wearing ponchos and trash bags with holes cut out for the arms and head, and puddles formed around the edges of the field.

Melton did not feel the conditions played any role in his arm issue.

"I've pitched in the cold and the rain before," Melton said. "It's not like it was something that super affected me. But yeah, honestly, the mound held up pretty well. It wasn't too bad."

Melton, in his second big-league season, had something of a coming-out party, entering Sunday with a 2.52 ERA over 110⅔ innings with 90 strikeouts and 34 walks.

title: Packers win bizarre overtime game despite almost impossible offensive stat
description: Green Bay produced only one successful third-down conversion and fewer than 200 yards, yet somehow escaped with a victory.
fullText:
Packers win bizarre overtime game despite almost impossible offensive stat originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Green Bay Packers appeared to have almost no business winning Sunday's game against the New York Jets. They won it anyway. Green Bay rallied from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit and defeated New York 20-17 in overtime on rookie Trey Smack's 26-yard field goal.

The comeback was remarkable because of what the Packers overcame.

Green Bay finished with only 199 total yards and converted one of nine third-down opportunities, according to the game recap. The Packers committed costly penalties, lost multiple players to injuries and spent most of the afternoon struggling to sustain a drive.

They still scored the final 13 points.

"That was a great way to finish," Jordan Love said in his postgame interview.

It was also one of the strangest victories Green Bay will have all season.

The Jets led 17-7 with slightly more than 11 minutes remaining. Love responded by leading Green Bay on a touchdown drive capped by his 3-yard pass to Christian Watson. Skyy Moore then produced a 63-yard kickoff return that helped set up Smack's tying 34-yard field goal.

Green Bay's defense took control in overtime.

The Packers sacked Geno Smith twice on New York's possession and forced a punt. Love then completed a 15-yard pass to Chris Brooks, while a late-hit penalty moved Green Bay deeper into Jets territory.

Smack converted the winning kick without hesitation.

The rookie's composure mattered because Green Bay's afternoon was filled with chaos. The Packers lost Jayden Reed to a neck injury and Zach Bako-Bewele to a knee injury. They were penalized repeatedly in a game that featured 27 accepted flags between the teams.

Green Bay also struggled to run its conventional offense. Love threw two touchdown passes, but the Packers rarely stayed on the field long enough to develop rhythm.

MORE: Caleb Williams injury overshadows Bears' brutal loss to Vikings

Matt LaFleur gave the defense considerable credit afterward.

"I can't give enough credit to our defense," LaFleur said through the Packers' official postgame coverage.

New York managed only three points after building its 17-7 lead. Breece Hall was limited to 29 rushing yards, taking away the element that should have allowed the Jets to protect their advantage.

The overtime possession was even more impressive.

Green Bay knew Smith had to pass and still found a way to reach him twice before the Jets could approach scoring range.

The Packers improved to 1-1 after a disappointing opener. The performance was far from clean, but the result prevented Green Bay from falling into an early hole.

Teams rarely win NFL games with fewer than 200 yards, one third-down conversion and a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit. Green Bay checked every box and still left MetLife Stadium victorious.

That might not be a repeatable formula. It was enough for one unforgettable afternoon.

title: Fortaleza beat Bahia, edge ahead in Copa do Nordeste Sub-20 final
description: Fortaleza defeated Bahia 1-0 on Sunday afternoon (20) at Estádio Presidente Vargas, in Fortaleza, in the first leg of the Copa do Nordeste U-20 final, and took the lead in the race for the title. Luc...
fullText:
Fortaleza defeated Bahia 1-0 on Sunday afternoon (20) at Estádio Presidente Vargas, in Fortaleza, in the first leg of the Copa do Nordeste U-20 final, and took the lead in the race for the title. Lucas Emanoel, in the 13th minute of the first half, scored the winning goal for Leão do Pici.

The result leaves the Ceará side needing only a draw to win a third title in the tournament. Esquadrão de Aço, meanwhile, needs a one-goal victory in the return leg to take the decision to penalties, and a win by two or more goals to be crowned two-time champion within the 90 minutes.

Fortaleza won the Copa do Nordeste U-20 in 2005 and 2018, while Bahia won the inaugural edition in 2001.

title: Raiders lose top rookie starter to concussion vs Chargers
description: Midway through the Raiders win over the Chargers Sunday they lost their starting rookie safety to a concussion.
fullText:
In the second quarter of the Raiders Week two game against the Chargers, Treydan Stukes made a tackle on special teams and left the game. Initial evaluations came up negative and he returned to the game for a drive and even make another tackle. But during half time, he apparently had further evaluations and soon was diagnosed with a concussion and was ruled out.

Coming in for him for the second half was veteran safety Isaiah Pola-Mao.

Stukes had won the team's starting safety job over Pola-Mao afer training camp. The rookie second round pick started and played every snap in the team's season opening win over the Miami Dolphins and record an interception in the game, making him the first Raiders rookie to do so in the his debut since 1982.

Luckily for the Raiders, it was an easy transition for Pola-Mao to step in. But there's a reason Stukes was named the starter because he was considered an upgrade at the position, so his loss is not insignificant.

Concussions can vary greatly so he will be monitored throughout the week to see if he can return for the Raiders Week three game in New Orleans.

title: Rodman gets a goal and an assist in the Spirit's 3-0 victory on the road against the Stars
description: Trinity Rodman scored in the seventh minute and added a late assist in the visiting Washington Spirit’s 3-0 victory over the Chicago Stars on Sunday.  In the day’s other National Women’s Soccer League matches, the Houston Dash edged the Boston Legacy 2-1, Angel City FC shut out the Utah Royals 3-0, and Bay FC defeated Racing Louisville 2-0.  Rodman provided an early spark, lifting a shot over Stars goalkeeper Alyssa Naeher in the seventh minute.
fullText:
Trinity Rodman scored in the seventh minute and added a late assist in the visiting Washington Spirit's 3-0 victory over the Chicago Stars on Sunday.

In the day's other National Women's Soccer League matches, the Houston Dash edged the Boston Legacy 2-1, Angel City FC shut out the Utah Royals 3-0, and Bay FC defeated Racing Louisville 2-0.

Rodman provided an early spark, lifting a shot over Stars goalkeeper Alyssa Naeher in the seventh minute. She sealed the win 78 minutes later, sending a lofted cross to Tamara Bolt's head for Washington's final goal.

Andi Sullivan doubled the Spirit's lead from the penalty spot in the 34th minute after Chicago's Bea Franklin was called for a handball in the box. Sullivan placed the kick into the bottom left corner.

Chicago (5-18-2) outshot Washington 5-4 despite the Spirit (14-7-4) controlling nearly 60% of possession.

The Houston Dash snapped a four-game winless streak with a 2-1 victory over the Boston Legacy at Centreville Bank Stadium in Rhode Island.

Sunday's match was Houston's first under interim head coach Jaime Frias.

Kylah Harper delivered the winning ball to Messiah Bright in the 85th minute. Bright's header slipped past goalkeeper Casey Murphy for her first goal of the season.

Boston (7-13-5) kept the pressure on Houston (8-12-5) throughout the match, forcing Dash goalkeeper Jane Campbell to make 10 saves.

Houston opened the scoring in the 44th minute when Danielle Colaprico capitalized on a frenzy in the box and put the loose ball past Murphy.

The Legacy equalized 15 minutes later. Nicki Hernández fired a cross toward Aïssata Traoré, who, playing on a yellow card, beat the Dash defenders to the ball and scored for the fifth consecutive game.

Utah (13-9-3) was left severely short-handed against Angel City after defender Paige Cronin and midfielder Ana Tejada were ejected by the 24th minute.

Two minutes later, Ally Sentnor converted the resulting penalty kick past goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn to put Angel City (11-8-6) ahead in Sandy, Utah.

Just two minutes after coming off the bench for the second half, Taylor Suarez made it 2-0 with a one-touch finish off a pass from Gisele Thompson.

Sveindís Jónsdóttir capped the scoring in the 67th minute, dispossessing Tatumn Milazzo deep in Utah territory before rolling a shot past McGlynn's right side.

Despite a slow start in San Jose, California, Bay FC scored twice in the opening 11 minutes of the second half to defeat Racing Louisville 2-0.

Bay (7-13-5) broke through in the 50th minute when Alex Pfeiffer converted a cross from Racheal Kundananji after Kundananji won the ball. Six minutes later, Racing Louisville (7-16-2) failed to clear another Kundananji cross, allowing Karlie Lema to finish.

The match also featured two milestones for Bay. Goalkeeper Jordan Silkowitz recorded her 100th save of the season in the 82nd minute, becoming the sixth player in league history to reach the mark in a single season. Maddie Moreau made her 50th appearance for the club when she entered as a substitute in the 84th minute.

title: Iran and U.S. trade threats after Houthi attacks escalate regional conflict.
description:
Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian ‌military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack. 
   The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready ‌for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilled over into new regional escalations. 
   In a phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump ​said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said. 
   However, with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added. 
   Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, without carrying them out.
fullText:
DUBAI/WASHINGTON, Sept 20 (Reuters) - Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian ‌military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack.

The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready ‌for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilled over into new regional escalations.

In a phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump ​said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said.

However, with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added.

Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, without carrying them out.

Earlier, Iran's military central command said any new attack would trigger sustained ‌retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington's ⁠regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict.

The Iranian military added that it had information that an attack was being prepared, without elaborating on what that information might be.

US Gulf allies have already been badly scarred by a ⁠war that the US and Israel launched with no warning, bringing their cities under Iranian fire and hammering their economies with the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway blockaded.

On Saturday their predicament worsened further, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group launching missile and drone strikes at the Saudi capital after having made sudden military gains in Yemen's reignited civil war ​earlier ​this month.

The US State Department ‌issued a security alert citing the Houthi hostilities. It said there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East, and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.

Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom.

Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure.

The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces ‌now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between ​the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway.

With Iran already ​having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's ​energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on oil prices.

A US blockade of ‌Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, ​contributing to major problems in the Islamic ​Republic's economy.

Despite the economic damage, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but fell apart in July amid disputes over its terms.

Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms ​of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met.

Iranian ‌Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies ​and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

title: ICE agent shoots and wounds man in Austin, authorities say
description:
— A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man Sunday afternoon in Austin, Texas, local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene.
The man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the capital city's north side, Austin officials said at a news conference. 
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not participate in the news conference and didn’t respond to repeated requests for details.
fullText:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man Sunday afternoon in Austin, Texas, local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene.

The man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the capital city's north side, Austin officials said at a news conference.

The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not participate in the news conference and didn't respond to repeated requests for details.

City police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said while briefing reporters along with the city's mayor and other officials.

Mayor Kirk Watson, a Democrat, said he wants the city's police department to have a role in the investigation so it can provide "clear, third-party eyes" in the process. Watson said he does not think it would be appropriate for ICE to conduct an investigation on its own.

Austin residents have "a right to feel safe in their city," Watson said. A proper investigation will only enhance credibility, he added.

The chief said there were not many facts she could provide so soon after the incident but added that her department's special investigation unit was at the scene.

The Texas Department of Public Safety said it received a request from ICE for assistance in a vehicle pursuit around 12:50 p.m. By the time DPS troopers arrived, the shooting had already taken place, the department said in a statement Sunday evening.

An immigration attorney representing the man's family identified him as Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan man.

Attorney Kate Lincoln Goldfinch said in a video posted to her Instagram account that she believed he had no criminal history and no final order of removal from the U.S., but she later told The Associated Press that she did not know his current immigration status.

The man's family has struggled to get any information from the hospital about his status or location, Lincoln-Goldfinch said.

Just before 7 p.m., the man's wife was informed by the hospital's attorney that the man had been released into ICE custody a few hours earlier, Lincoln-Goldfinch wrote in a text to AP.

"No one bothered to update her," she wrote.

It wasn't immediately clear if the man remained hospitalized while in ICE custody or if he had been transferred elsewhere.

A dark blue Toyota Corolla was parked under an overpass with damage to its passenger-side door and what appeared to be bullet holes. The car was towed away in the early evening and traffic began moving again.

A large law enforcement presence was present along with a crowd of about a hundred protesters. Some demonstrators cursed at police officers holding riot shields, while others yelled out as passing cars honked in support of the protest. One man held a sign saying, "Nobody is safe" and, on the other side, "ICE Nazi."

Asked if Austin authorities knew where the involved federal agent is, given that agents have left states after previous shootings nationwide, the mayor said: "We do not know that. But my hope would be that, an agent that's involved in an officer-involved shooting would not leave the city. Certainly not leave the state."

The office of Travis County District Attorney José Pompa Garza asked that local police and prosecutors be included in the investigation.

"We further request cooperation from the federal government in giving us access to the evidence," the DA's office said in a statement Sunday evening.

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, a Democrat representing parts of Austin, called for transparency as the shooting is investigated.

"It is awful that this horror has come to our doorstep," Casar told reporters. "For Austin to be safe, ICE should end its surge here."

The shooting comes as ICE surges enforcement across the country this summer, producing more than 50,000 arrests a month for the first time in its history in July and August.

In July, an ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, of Houston, after federal agents driving unmarked vehicles pursued him while he was taking his construction crew to a job site.

Also in July, 25-year-old Johan Sebastián, a Colombian man, was shot by an ICE officer in Maine. The officer is an Army veteran who has struggled with serious mental health issues since early childhood and never should have been given a badge and gun to patrol American streets, several of his close relatives told AP.

The administration's enforcement efforts were widely condemned last winter after the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota.

Weber reported from Los Angeles and Boone from Boise, Idaho. Contributing were Associated Press journalists Kimberlee Kruesi in Providence, Rhode Island and Tim Sullivan in Minneapolis.

title: 'He died in my arms': Patrick Clancy opens up about the grief of losing 3 children
description:
Patrick Clancy said he felt he had no purpose after his three children were killed.
"There was a time where I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday," Clancy, 36, said in an interview with 60 Minutes. "And I was completely fine with it."
His interview with correspondent Ross Douthat comes after his ex-wife's mistrial earlier this month. The court has yet to determine whether Patrick's ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy, will be retried for the killings of their children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan.
fullText:
Patrick Clancy said he felt he had no purpose after his three children were killed.

"There was a time where I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday," Clancy, 36, said in an interview with 60 Minutes. "And I was completely fine with it."

His interview with correspondent Ross Douthat comes after his ex-wife's mistrial earlier this month. The court has yet to determine whether Patrick's ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy, will be retried for the killings of their children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. It also comes as Patrick and his wife, Rachel Danis, face intense public scrutiny, becoming the subjects of online suspicion and speculation on social media.

In October 2022, five months after Callan's birth, Patrick said Lindsay told him she had gone a few nights without sleeping.

Over the next two months, Lindsay made repeated emergency room visits. She admitted herself to a program for patients with postpartum depression and was discharged after a day of treatment. Lindsay was also prescribed an escalating number of prescription drugs.

Patrick said he struggled to help his wife navigate the medical system and did not know how to manage a postpartum illness.

"I think mental illness has this ability to be tragically deceptive," he said.

December was the low point, Patrick said. "It was a big struggle for her — just a huge lack of sleep, deep, deep depression, intrusive thoughts."

Lindsay checked herself into McLean Psychiatric Hospital on New Year's Eve. She was treated for depression and released days later, making it home in time to celebrate Cora's birthday on Jan. 7.

Less than three weeks later, Patrick said he came home from an errand to find Lindsay lying in the backyard, her throat and wrists cut, paralyzed after jumping from an upstairs window.

He said he found his children strangled in the basement. Cora and Dawson were dead. Callan was airlifted to Boston Children's Hospital.

"I really thought there was a chance that Callan would live," Patrick recalled. "I remember just thinking, 'Just give me one. Just give me one kid, and I would raise him as best I could, and I would give him the best life I possibly could. I'd tell him about his brother and sister.' And I was holding out hope for that."

Callan's heart kept beating for four days.

"I got to hold him. I got to lay down next to him. And he died in my arms," Patrick said.

Patrick Clancy forgives his ex-wife

In the days after the tragedy, Patrick wrote tributes to each of his three children and decided to publicly forgive Lindsay.

"I saw headlines that said, you know, 'Killer Mom,' and 'Baby Murderer,' 'Monster.' And none of them were accurate," Patrick said. "I think if people said, 'She did a horrible thing,' I think everyone could agree with that. …But I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that." So I shared those words."

Lindsay never asked for forgiveness, but Patrick said he gave it to her. They've both brought medical malpractice lawsuits against health care providers who treated Lindsay. Some have denied wrongdoing, and others have yet to respond to the claim.

Patrick said he thinks he "did the best I could with what I had at the time. And I live with the outcome. I live with it every day."

Patrick said he realized he could no longer stay in Duxbury and moved to New York City that April, seeking anonymity.

Trial in court — and in the court of public opinion

In July, Lindsay Clancy's trial began. Her lawyers argued she was suffering from dangerous postpartum psychosis and couldn't be held criminally responsible for her actions.

The trial became a national obsession – generating furious arguments about the relationship between mental illness and criminal fault, how the medical system fails mothers and how men and women understand one another.

Patrick testified and found himself at the center of an online swarm of sleuths and influencers dissecting every detail of the case, developing theories that portray him as uncaring, unfaithful and even the murderer of his children.

"It's painful to see. And it makes it difficult to be in public and it's possible that some of those people, after seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it and that's what we're left with," he said.

One of the catalysts for the theories about Patrick was his apparent stoicism on the witness stand. Patrick said that testifying was difficult for him and that he had a "massive, traumatic" panic attack on the second day of his testimony.

"They put me in an ambulance," Patrick said. "They offered me some medication, but I said, 'I don't want it, because I want to go back and I want to finish this so I can be done with this.' And I went back and I finished the testimony."

Lindsay's trial ended with a hung jury earlier this month.

Patrick says reaching out to survivors and experts in the field of postpartum health has helped him move forward. He remarried this April to Dr. Rachel Danis, a fertility doctor in New York City.

Danis said the pair met in January 2024 in a New York City run club and got to know each other over coffee.

"Pat pulled out his phone to pay, and I noticed this adorable photo of children as the wallpaper," Danis said. " I just asked, 'Who are those cuties?' And Pat said, 'Those are my kids.' And then I think I asked if they live in Massachusetts, and Pat said, 'They died.' And this is just at the cashier."

Danis said she tried to "take some of the weight from Pat."

"I can't bring his kids back," she said. "But if I can honor them and allow Pat to grieve but also just continue to honor them in the present, it, I guess that's all I can do."

The pair are starting a family, and Patrick is preparing to one day tell his future child about their older siblings, Cora, Dawson and Callan.

"I think every parent can agree, you have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids," he said. "And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister."

title: Yu, 13, wins record-breaking first major gold medal
description: China’s Yu Zidi, 13, wins a record‑breaking 200m women’s butterfly gold at the Asian Games in Tokyo.
fullText:
Chinese schoolgirl Yu Zidi lit up the opening day of the Asian Games with a record‑breaking 200m butterfly gold medal secured by a performance she described as "only so‑so".

The 13‑year‑old claimed her first major gold in two minutes 05.08 seconds, an Asian Games record that took almost half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei's mark from three years ago.

Yu, who is strongly tipped to make an impact at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, won by over three seconds in Tokyo from her team-mate Chang Mohan.

"It was only so-so," a smiling Yu said after receiving her medal, adding that her butterfly technique "is still slightly lacking".

"I hope I can swim even faster. I improved my time by 0.9 seconds here, and I believe I will perform better next time," she continued.

Yu, who will take part in two more individual events at the Asian Games, became the youngest ever swimmer to win a medal at the World Championships when she took bronze as a 12-year-old as part of China's 4x200m freestyle relay team last year.

title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

fullText:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa): He let in two against Spurs but that was when Villa decided they weren't really going to try any more so no pressure on him for those goals.

He commanded his area and has really taken to the Premier League quickly. No real change considering Emiliano Martinez has left. He came and took the ball a lot.

Jay Dasilva (Coventry): He got their first goal in the Premier League for 25 years. He gets the winning goal, you go in at right-back for that.

Luka Vuskovic (Brighton): I was at that game against Arsenal. Dominant defender but also very good on the ball. It doesn't get spoken about how much he puts aggressive pressure on the ball, goes into midfield to win the ball back and he's calm.

Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool): Best player on the pitch by a mile against Bournemouth. Young, fast, aggressive but also really calm when he gets the ball.

Lewis Hall (Newcastle): Goals, assists, keeps getting better. After Manchester United playing the way they did against Fulham you wonder how did they not spend the money on getting him in.

Antoine Semenyo (Man City): Two goals and an assist. He looks to be playing a little more carefree with manager Enzo Maresca and that's the small details between the Italian and his predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Guardiola is trying to tell you what to do with every single action.

Joe Willock (Newcastle): He's really coming out of his shell this season. Like a few players, previous boss Eddie Howe used him sparingly but now he's playing week in, week out. A few injuries mean he's the main man again in midfield. High energy, goals, just that ability to take people on and drag you 50 yards up the pitch is amazing.

Chema Andres (Brighton): They suffocated Arsenal in midfield. I wanted to make Fabian Hurzeler my manager because of their unbelievable tactics. Andres must have won the ball back off Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Odegaard at least 15 times. He was so good in his positioning and possession and he got a goal.

Johan Manzambi (Aston Villa): You see why Villa paid the money they did for him. Unreal for Freiburg last season. He hasn't really had any time due to injury but he comes in to the eam and gets one goal, one assist in his first start. Unreal.

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland): He gets a hat-trick against Manchester City. Even though they lost he comes away with a lot of credit. He won't want the international break to come because he's been doing really well for Sunderland.

Charalampos Kostoulas (Brighton): Goal, assist, excellent link-up play. He is physically really good and was a real nuisance against Arsenal.

The injury to Georginio Rutter and Danny Welbeck leaving has given the Greek teenager the freedom to feel comfortable in Brighton's starting XI.

Keith Andrews (Brentford): I can't get a Brentford player in the team despite them beating Chelsea 3-0. Unbelievable performance. Andrews keeps that momentum going so that's why he's manager of the week. Unbelievable start for him.

title: Neville calls Man Utd 'pathetic' - but Carrick maintains belief
description: Gary Neville calls Manchester United "pathetic", but boss Michael Carrick maintains belief after salvaging draw at Fulham.
fullText:
Gary Neville took a deep breath after Lisandro Martinez's own goal put Fulham ahead just over an hour into what had been a laboured Manchester United performance, and delivered his verdict.

The former United skipper is never short of a scathing word, but even by his standards, this was brutal.

"I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen," he said. "Absolutely pathetic.

"I've never seen such a lack of effort. What must [Michael] Carrick be thinking?"

For context, Neville was part of the United side beaten 3-1 by Sunday's opponents Fulham at Old Trafford in October 2003. In recent memory they have also lost 7-0 at Liverpool and 6-1 at home twice, to Tottenham and Manchester City.

Neville's words came after a poor quarter of an hour from the start of the second half to Martinez's moment of ill fortune, before United went on to snatch a 1-1 draw thanks to Matheus Cunha's deflected strike in the 89th minute.

It seemed an extreme reaction. But in a week when United lost the Manchester derby to a City side reduced to 10 men midway through the first half, then against Brighton for the first time in more than 50 years were beaten at home after giving away a two-goal lead, frustration among the fanbase is high.

Questions over fitness were first raised during pre-season when midfielder Youri Tielemans revealed United were not prioritising running.

While Cunha did not exactly agree with Neville in his post-match interview with Sky Sports, his comments will have fuelled more debate around the issue.

"At the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us," said the Brazilian. "We cannot accept this."

Unsurprisingly, Carrick had a different take. He used the way his side tried to pressure the home team in the latter stages, leading to Cunha's equaliser, as evidence his squad is fit enough.

"The way we finished the game, actually, it didn't look like that. We finished the game really strong actually, and kept pushing. I don't think that's an issue, no," he said.

Cunha also mentioned the "noise" around United when he spoke to BBC Match of the Day.

Neville is a significant part of that noise, either directly or through his growing media empire.

Carrick has previously said he can shut it out.

It cannot be quite so easy though when United fans - who usually back their team through disappointment - followed up chants on Wednesday in disgust at the Brighton debacle by here booing Carrick's decision to take off popular England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo 11 minutes from time.

"There's always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," said Carrick. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.

"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are, as well they should be, desperate for us to do the right thing.

"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.

"The supporters were unbelievable today, I have to say, all the way through, and stuck with the boys and supported them. At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

A draw at Fulham is "something small" considering the home side started the game at the foot of the Premier League - and have now swapped places with Tottenham.

Five points from five games leaves United 12th, an incredible 10 points behind pacesetters Manchester City already.

Their £70m summer signing Carlos Baleba is still to make his debut, and long-term injury victim Matthijs de Ligt was not involved at all, even though both were part of the squad that travelled south on Saturday.

Striker Benjamin Sesko also missed the game after suffering a recurrence of the shin problem against Brighton that he was troubled by for an extended period last season before submitting to a recovery programme that ruled him out for more than three months.

Carrick says "at this point" the extent of the damage is unknown.

This would all be pretty underwhelming were it not for the ticketing issues instigated by the club's touting crackdown that has annoyed so many in the fanbase.

On Wednesday, United will release their full-year financial results to 30 June, around which the full extent of their current debt will be revealed.

Then there is the general debate about the wisdom of new stadium, which is set to cost in excess of £2bn, with planning permission potentially submitted with the main Old Trafford masterplan, which is earmarked for late 2027 or early 2028.

Little wonder, after leading United back to the Champions League so unexpectedly last season, Carrick is presiding over a club whose supporters feel deflated, even if he does not recognise that.

"It's still a big season ahead," he said. "It's a long season and you're going to have spells through a season. That's part of the journey.

"It's not a sprint, it's a long effort.

"I'm not playing it down, you know. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better and we wanted to do other things.

"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch today and that's what will carry us through the season without a doubt."

title: Elvira loses nerve as Spaun triumphs at Wentworth
description: Manuel Elvira choked back the tears as an elated JJ Spaun celebrated becoming only the third US player to win the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
fullText:
BMW PGA Championship - final round

-17 JJ Spaun (US); -15 M Elvira (Spa), R McIlroy (NI), A Scott (Aus), A Rai (Eng)

Selected others:-14 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), R Fox (NZ); -13 R MacIntyre (Sco), M Wallace (Eng), A Sullivan (Eng); -12 A Noren (Swe), R Fisher (Eng); -11 S Lowry (Ire) A Fitzpatrick (Eng); -10 V Hovland (Nor), L Aberg (Swe), J Niemann (Chi), T Hatton (Eng)

Golf can be a cruel game. As Spain's Manuel Elvira choked back the tears on Sunday, just a short distance away an elated JJ Spaun celebrated becoming only the third player from the United States to win the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.

The 2025 US Open champion joins Billy Horschel and the legendary Arnold Palmer on a storied list of winners that also includes Tony Jacklin, Sir Nick Faldo, Seve Ballesteros, Jose Maria Olazabal and Rory McIlroy.

However, it was hard not to feel sympathy for Elvira, the unknown 30-year-old from Santander.

Ranked 294th in the world, this had looked like being the moment he had longed for when he stepped on to the final tee with a first victory in his sights - straight off the back of outrageous eagle on the 17th.

Having twice made birdies on the friendly par five this week, a third was hardly implausible - while a par would have ensured a play-off with Spaun, already in the clubhouse at 17 under par.

Instead Elvira, who opted for an iron off the tee, found a fairway bunker when he took the conservative option to lay up.

To compound matters he then missed the green with his approach, almost finding the grandstand, and duffed his fourth into the sand after being given a free drop.

Once he escaped he took a further two putts, and his double-bogey seven finish deprived him of even ending the tournament in outright second place.

"[It was] devastating that I hit the wrong shot at the right time on the lay up and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker, and wasn't able to pull it off," Elvira said.

"I've played some of the best golf probably of my life."

While it was not at the level of Jean Van de Velde's implosion at the 1999 Open Championship or, more recently, Jordan Spieth's misadventures in the 2016 Masters - it nevertheless made for difficult viewing.

And his brother Ignacio - who had earlier finished in a tie for 44th - was left to console his younger sibling as they walked off the 18th green.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, former Europe Solheim Cup player Trish Johnson said: "It's a truly awful feeling. No more than 20 minutes ago he's got this huge dream.

"To watch that unfold on 18 was really, in golfing terms, quite tragic. What he has to remember is how he put himself in that position.

"In a big event like this the chances are we'll never see him in that position to win this calibre of tournament ever again, and that's very sad."

As Elvira trudged away after ending on 15 under alongside major champions McIlroy, Adam Scott and Aaron Rai, which in any other circumstances could have been considered a triumph, Spaun was already rejoicing his first title outside of the US.

While that will earn him a hefty pay cheque of about £1.1m, he said his omission from the US Presidents Cup - a tournament where America face a rest-of-the-world team, excluding Europe - had been the driving force behind his success.

Spaun outlined that he had been given the news in a 45-second phone call, in which he was told he was the "odd man out".

"I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week but everything happens for a reason," said Spaun, who carded a five-under 67 on Sunday, crucially including four birdies in the concluding five holes.

"My whole career, I've kind of had to do that. I wasn't given scholarships. I had a walk-on. I had to earn my PGA Tour card the hard way. I was never given sponsor invite opportunities. I just had to do everything the hard way.

"Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing, and you know, I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team."

One amusing aspect of Spaun's round was seeing his wife Melody walking around the grounds of the famous Surrey club with a Jeremy Clarkson mask.

"We've grown fond of him - along with the English culture, we actually take holidays in December in the Cotswolds - and we really enjoy his show [Clarkson's Farm]," Spaun added.

"I went to his pub, with the hopes of catching a glimpse of him, but he wasn't around.

"My wife said we would have a surprise guest following me this week if I competed in the tournament and, sure enough, I see the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it. Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune."

While Spaun's putter ran hot, McIlroy made five birdies and a bogey on Sunday, in a round that also included four birdie misses from inside 10 feet.

The one consolation for the six-time major winner is that he made a huge dent in Patrick Reed's lead in the Race to Dubai standings as he goes for a record-equalling eighth title.

"I'm excited. I have three events until the end of my DP World Tour season. I'm not sure what Patrick's schedule looks like coming up, but I feel like I have enough opportunities," McIlroy said.

"I'm excited for the opportunity, and it would be obviously amazing to match Monty's record."

title: What have we learned from the Premier League so far?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the opening weeks of the Premier League season as a long international break arrives.
fullText:
The Premier League takes a near three-week break as we enter a four-game international window.

So, what have we learned from the opening five matches of the season?

Premier League champions Arsenal were looking fairly unstoppable in the opening weeks of the season.

A win over Brighton on Saturday would have given the Gunners a club-record equalling eighth consecutive win in all competitions to start the season.

But that all ended with a 3-0 loss at Amex Stadium on Saturday.

The Gunners had not lost a league game by more than one goal, let alone three, since October 2024.

It was their heaviest defeat in the league since May 2023 when they lost 3-0 to the same opposition.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," said boss Mikel Arteta.

"What we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable - but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

Many wondered if Manchester City would experience a post-Pep Guardiola slump when the legendary boss left after a decade.

Things did not start too well under Enzo Maresca, with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

But they have won all five games in the Premier League - and seven in a row in all competitions - after Sunday's entertaining 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That takes them three points clear of Arsenal.

"In the press conference before the game, I said I expect a very tough game," said Maresca. "Then we also conceded two or three goals but we have learned a lot in these eight weeks and this is good."

Perfect 24 hours as Man City put pressure on Arsenal

Brighton and Brentford, two clubs who have never won a major trophy, have continued to impress this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton enjoyed that 3-0 win over Arsenal to see them sit third in the table, only two points behind the Gunners.

Brighton have won at home against the reigning Premier League champions in each of the last three seasons.

Star player Pascal Gross laughed and said "no" when BBC Sport asked him if Albion were in the title race.

But stranger things have happened...

Meanwhile, just one point below them in the table are Keith Andrews' Brentford.

Many tipped the Bees to struggle after the departure of Thomas Frank last summer but if anything they improved under their former set-piece coach Andrews.

And their start to this season - unbeaten after five games and fourth in the table - is showing he is no one-season wonder as a manager.

They go into the break on the back of their most impressive result, a 3-0 home win over Chelsea.

Leeds, impressing again under boss Daniel Farke, are also on nine points and in a potential Champions League place.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool and Everton are just below them on goal difference.

From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style

Seven years apart, United did the same thing twice hoping for different results - appointing a club legend who last managed in Britain in the Championship after a good start as caretaker boss.

In 2019 it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and this time it was Michael Carrick.

But this season, after Carrick having a summer to work on his team, the Red Devils have only won once in the league.

Their five points after five league games is their joint fewest at this stage of a Premier League season.

They go into the international break on the back of a 1-1 draw against Fulham, and even needed a late deflected Matheus Cunha strike to stop the Cottagers winning their first game all season.

After the Lisandro Martinez own goal that give Fulham the lead, ex-United captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort."

United's owners will have almost three weeks to stew on this before they host fellow underachievers Tottenham (more on them soon) on 10 October.

In 2024 and 2025, the three promoted teams went straight back down - mostly with really low points tallies too.

But that streak came to an end last year when Sunderland finished seventh to qualify for Europe and Leeds came 14th. Only Burnley went down.

And the early weeks of this season indicate we could be in for a similar situation.

Hull City are eighth after five games, with their 2-1 loss to Newcastle their first defeat.

Ipswich are 11th. And Coventry, after losing the first four games without scoring, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and only sit in the drop zone on goal difference.

A Coventry win 25 years in the making

Tottenham finished 17th the last two seasons, their lowest two finishes since being in the second tier in 1977-78.

But expectations were raised after a summer of big spending - with Spurs splashing out £302m as well as making two high-profile loan signings.

Defence and midfield in particular were overhauled, with new wingers too.

But they are left with one senior striker in Dominic Solanke, who has only scored 12 Premier League goals in over two years at the club.

"I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle," said TNT pundit and ex-England international Joe Cole.

Saturday's 3-2 loss against Aston Villa sees them sit 19th going into the break - despite scoring their first two league goals of the campaign.

"We have to put on the pitch something more than we are putting," said manager Roberto de Zerbi.

"Football is tactical but it is blood, it is fighting, it is first one on the ball. We will suffer until the next game."

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Many were keen to see what Xabi Alonso could do at Chelsea this season.

The Spaniard memorably led Bayer Leverkusen to a historic unbeaten German double in 2023-24.

And they made big changes to their squad this summer, with £117m attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers and new first-choice keeper Emiliano Martinez both coming in from Aston Villa.

There have been 22 goals in their five league games - more coming against them than for them - and they sit 10th.

And that is not even counting the 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Hugely entertaining for the neutrals - but perhaps not for Chelsea fans or management.
